## 19\. Findings inside Sŏn's record

Thirteen findings, each a conflict, a silence, or two accounts of the same thing, found by reading the white paper and both canon artifacts against each other with diagnosis, change, departure, and rebuilding as the question. The ledger's open questions and Sessions 5 to 8's findings (the six-tier difference, the data hub, the cultural labor score's single line, the advancement gate's two accounts at S6 18.2, the how-versus-operational-work line at S8 21.6, the founders as destinations at S8 21.11) are not counted again; where one touches a finding it is named as adjacent. None is resolved here; where a section above supplied a working answer, the finding says which position holds it and marks it as the team's reading.

**19.1 The machine has four failure modes and the diagnostic has five, and memory failure is the one that does not carry across.** In one place: "CPU failure... Memory failure... Bus failure... Cooling failure" (WP p.13), with memory failure as "Institutional knowledge lives in people, not in the system. Every departure takes knowledge with it." Elsewhere, on the next page: the reference names tension slack, node overload, sequence corruption, skill invisibility, and cooling failure (WP p.14), and no mode for knowledge leaving with a person; CPU failure reads as node overload, bus failure as sequence corruption, cooling as cooling, and memory failure has no twin. Why it bears on diagnosis: a departure is the event the record says the code-bearing structure survives (WP p.14), and the diagnostic has no line for the failure a departure exposes. Who closes: the record's author; section 9.1 reads the departure's knowledge loss under sequence corruption and skill invisibility as the team's reading. Silence, inside the narrow range.

**19.2 Node overload's fix is a separation between two seats, and the ruling puts the load's convergence inside one.** In one place: "The fix is restoring the Operations Lead and Maitre d separation" (WP p.14). Elsewhere: the ruling of 2026-09-13 makes the floor manager and the Maitre d one seat, and Session 8's pass found four disturbance classes converging on that seat with no regulator beneath it for the people-side class (S8 5.2). Why it bears on diagnosis: the record's only named fix for the mode most likely to be read on the floor is between two seats the ruling did not touch, and it says nothing for overload inside the seat it did. Who closes: the founders in ratifying section 12's carriers; the team's reading is that the separation is restored between the how and the operational work and the load beneath the seat is carried by designation, stack, or procedure. Adjacent to S8 21.6. Silence, inside the narrow range with the ledger.

**19.3 The reference is "a diagnostic against any operational problem," and the record names no one who runs it, no rhythm, and no record.** In one place: "Use this as a diagnostic" (WP p.14). Elsewhere: the record's only named reviewer of anything is "the appropriate lead reviews" a captured incident (WP p.13), and the only rhythms it names are the review every three to six months (WP p.19) and the pulse "regularly" (WP p.22); nothing says who applies the reference, when, or where the result is written. Why it bears on diagnosis: an instrument with no runner runs on a founder's memory, which is the mode it exists to catch. Who closes: the founders in ratifying section 4.2's writers and section 6's rhythms as the team's reading. Silence, inside the narrow range.

**19.4 Cooling failure's stated evidence includes retention, which the record elsewhere calls the X-ray.** In one place: cooling failure is read where "joy is absent, and retention is suffering" (WP p.14). Elsewhere: "Lagging indicators, revenue, labor cost, food cost, are the X-ray after the fracture" (WP p.12), and retention rate sits on the cultural measurement's quantitative side as evidence "the development commitments are real" (WP p.23), read over time rather than in the moment. Why it bears on diagnosis: the ledger forbids a diagnostic that opens with a lagging figure, and the record's own evidence list for one mode names one. Who closes: the record's author; section 4.7 reads retention as a count of tension-loss departures in the quarter, a leading form, and reads the pulse and the thermal-load lines first, as the team's reading. Two accounts; needs p.14 against pp. 12 and 23.

**19.5 A departure's cost is "calculable," and nothing in the record calculates it.** In one place: the departure is "a bounded, temporary, calculable one rather than a structural and compounding one" (WP p.14). Elsewhere: turnover's cost is "the tension that position was holding" (WP p.9), the return on culture includes "reduced turnover" (WP p.23), and no unit, owner, or method for the calculation appears anywhere; financials are not a context source for this program in any case. Why it bears on diagnosis: a diagnostic asked to show the cost falling "as the system holds more of what people know" (WP p.14) has to have a unit. Who closes: the founders, with Dominic's domain if the unit is money; section 9.1's unit, which mechanism now has to be maintained and which seats carry the load for how many services, is the team's reading. Silence; needs p.14 against pp. 9 and 23.

**19.6 The knowledge stays in the system, and the relationship leaves with the server.** In one place: on a departure "the knowledge does not leave. It lives in the system as documented processes, captured customer preferences" (WP p.14), and "that knowledge cannot live in a server's memory, because memory leaves when the server does" (WP p.27). Elsewhere: "Belonging is not to a building, it is to people," each server builds "their own book of regulars," and "if a server moves to another property in the group, their regulars may follow, because the belonging was always to the person, not just the place" (WP p.25). Why it bears on departure: the tension-loss row has to say what the node held, and the record holds that the customer relationship both stays in the layer and goes with the person. Who closes: the founders, with Session 11 for the customer-facing side; section 9.1 reads the preferences as the system's and the relationship as a compensation the adjacent seats carry, as the team's reading. Two accounts; needs p.14 and p.27 against p.25.

**19.7 Canon's training test is judgment, and the record's skill-invisibility fix is documentation.** In one place: the Playground Philosophy requires "training architecture that progresses from procedure mastery to autonomous judgment" and prohibits "training systems that measure procedure execution without building toward judgment" (Canon 1.0, section 01). Elsewhere: skill invisibility's fix is "documentation and system access" and the path is "documented competency requirements visible to anyone" (WP pp. 11, 14), with judgment nowhere in the mode's definition. Why it bears on diagnosis: a skill-invisibility line that reads only whether the path is documented would pass a path that documents procedures and never judgment, which canon forbids at tier 1 and tier 2. Who closes: canon's owner with the Curriculum seat; section 4.6 adds canon's test to the mode's read as the team's reading. Two accounts; canon against the white paper.

**19.8 The record changes the process nightly and the deck changes only by versioned decision.** In one place: "the process that allowed the failure gets updated, and the next server inherits a system that has already learned from it" (WP p.13), nightly, with no version step named. Elsewhere: "A living document changes by versioned decision, never by drift" (Deck 3.0, p.94), and Jaeyeonmi's "maintenance philosophy that distinguishes care from correction" (Canon 1.0, section 01). Why it bears on change: the record has an unversioned daily loop and a versioned rule, and never says which changes need a version; a diagnosis that produced only nightly updates would be drift by the deck's word, and one that versioned every capture would not run at tempo. Who closes: the founders, with canon's versioning authority (`86akh3t3y`); section 7.1's care-and-correction line is the team's reading. Two accounts; the white paper against both canon artifacts.

**19.9 Upward feedback and exit interviews have no reader and no path to the diagnostic.** In one place: "Feedback runs both directions. Team members weigh in on management effectiveness, operational improvements, and culture" (WP p.19), and "Exit interviews read for what could have been better rather than filed and forgotten" (WP p.23). Elsewhere: no seat is named to read either, no rhythm, and no destination; the team's read of a lead's effectiveness is the one signal that reads node overload from beneath the seat, and the exit interview is the one signal that reads cooling failure from someone who left. Why it bears on diagnosis: two of the diagnostic's most direct sources are committed and unrouted. Who closes: the founders, with `86akhb2jg` for the lead's side; section 4.7 reads exit interviews as building lines and section 4.4 reads the check-in's upward question as a source, as the team's reading. Silence; needs p.19 against p.23.

**19.10 Cross-training is everyone's career development, and the record says strand aptitude differs by person.** In one place: "Cross-training is career development, not only operational insurance. A server who learns the kitchen becomes more valuable everywhere" (WP p.19), and each person "develops outward, deeper into their domain and across into adjacent ones" (WP p.11). Elsewhere: "The best outward-facing operators may be mediocre in the inward-facing role, and the reverse" (WP p.10 to 11), and cross-strand fluency is "the rare person" (WP p.11). Why it bears on the career conversation and diagnosis: a person who does not cross strands has done nothing the record says everyone should, and a skill-invisibility line that read their unmoved fluency record as a path not visible would be wrong by the record's own strand claim. Who closes: the record's author; section 15.2 lets the person name a track inside their strand and section 4.6 reads only unscheduled forms, not un-taken tracks, as the team's reading. Two accounts; needs p.19 against pp. 10 and 11.

**19.11 Nunchi is "not diagnostic inquiry," and the reference is "a diagnostic."** In one place: Nunchi is "the intuitive reading of what someone needs before they ask. Not diagnostic inquiry. Not a checklist" (Canon 1.0, section 01; Deck 3.0, p.15). Elsewhere: "Use this as a diagnostic against any operational problem" (WP p.14), five named modes, a fix each, which is a checklist by form. Why it bears on diagnosis: the same word names the thing the floor must never do to a customer and the thing the house must do to itself, and a diagnostic that crossed into the room, a lead reading a person's state by inquiry at the brief, would violate canon at tier 3 by canon's own word. Who closes: canon's owner, for the vocabulary; section 2.1's rule that the diagnostic reads mechanisms and reaches a person only by section 14 is the team's reading. Language conflict; canon against the white paper.

**19.12 The invisible advocate is a seat's function and the system's mechanism, under one name.** In one place: the Maitre d owns "Team development, training, and the invisible advocate function" (WP p.10). Elsewhere: "The system is the advocate. No one's advancement waits on a manager's attention or judgment" (WP p.11). Why it bears on diagnosis: skill invisibility's fix has a seat owner if the function is the Maitre d's and no seat owner if the system is the advocate, and who writes the skill-invisibility line turns on it. Who closes: the founders, with the advancement wording ruling (`86akhcz22`); section 4.2 has the Maitre d write the floor's line and the stack's records supply it, as the team's reading. Two accounts; needs p.10 against p.11.

**19.13 Tension slack's compensation is "without visibility," and the nervous system is what feels early.** In one place: in tension slack "other nodes are compensating without visibility" (WP p.14). Elsewhere: the stack "allows the organization to feel what a restaurant without it cannot feel, early enough to respond rather than repair" (WP p.12). Why it bears on diagnosis: the record says the one mode whose read can reach a person is the one mode the nervous system as built does not see, so its evidence has to be constructed from records the stack captures for other reasons. Who closes: the record's author; section 4.3's sources (the close's cross-section range use, the adjacent seats' own lines, the schedule's re-sectioning) are the team's construction of that visibility. Two accounts; needs p.14 against p.12.

Thirteen findings: five silences, six two-account conflicts, one language conflict, and one two-account conflict inside the narrow range with the ledger. Three of the thirteen (19.1, 19.2, 19.3) sit inside WP pp. 13 to 14 or in p.14 against the ledger's ruling and would surface from a narrow read of the failure mode reference against its own source. The other ten would not: 19.4 needs p.14 against pp. 12 and 23; 19.5 needs p.14 against pp. 9 and 23; 19.6 needs Part I against Part III twice over; 19.7, 19.8, and 19.11 need canon against the white paper, and 19.8 both canon artifacts; 19.9 needs p.19 against p.23; 19.10 needs p.19 against pp. 10 and 11; 19.12 needs p.10 against p.11; 19.13 needs p.14 against p.12. A session that read the failure mode reference and stopped would have drawn the five modes and missed that one of them cites a lagging measure, that the departure it promises to bound has no unit and loses the relationship the record says compounds, that the documentation fix fails canon's judgment test, and that the word "diagnostic" is the word canon uses for what the floor must never do.

**P51 (Recommended).** The thirteen findings are filed as stated, each routed to who closes it. None is resolved here; where a section above supplied a working answer it is the team's reading and marked as such. 19.1, 19.3, 19.4, 19.5, 19.10, and 19.13 are routed to the record's author with the team's reading; 19.2, 19.9, and 19.12 to the founders with the open items they extend; 19.6 to the founders and Session 11; 19.7, 19.8, and 19.11 to canon's owner and the versioning authority.

Fifty-one positions: forty-four recommended, two founder-gated, two chef-gated, three team-filled. Twelve readiness rows, 107 to 118; the test stands at one hundred and eighteen. Nine instruments used and nine refused, absorbed, or replaced. Thirteen findings.

**Founder-gated.** P35, the diagnosis of a lead's node, held on who holds a lead's check-in (`86akhb2jg`). P47, the incomplete decision-rights entries: the lead's holder, the threshold values (Dominic's domain), the allocation consequence (`86akh3t00`), the cultural labor score's line (`86akh5u9x`), the interim two-partner rule (`86akh5u77`), the inventory's owner (`86akh7qq4`), and Session 14's read of a hire that does not hold. The founders also ratify the recommended positions on which the instrument's shape turns: P1 and P4 (the frame and the order), P8 (the line's form), P17 (the thresholds), P25 and P26 (the paths and the read-back), P36 (the seat's carriers), P41 and P42 (the one path to a person and the refusal to write), and P43 and P44 (the career conversation).

**What the founders and the chef must close, in the order the gates need them.**

1. Who holds a lead's check-in (`86akhb2jg`), before the leads are in the building six weeks ahead of dinner's gate, because the leads' own lines and the career conversation for a lead cannot be written without it, and row 118 fails until it closes.
2. The owner of the seat inventory (`86akh7qq4`), before the first structure change entry, because every path in section 7 writes on it.
3. The data hub of record (`86akh5u6e`), before I1 and I3 are built, because the lines and the surfacing rules live on whatever holds the role.
4. The chef seat ruling (`86akh2qrp`), before the kitchen's lines, its career conversation, and its decision-rights entries exist at all.
5. The cultural labor score's definition (`86akh5u9x`), before the first house review, so that cooling failure's line reads it rather than carrying "cannot read yet" into the first reset.
6. "The order is the decision" (`86akh3t00`), before the first hold-open slack reading and the first cooling-failure fix, because what the fix may cost is not the team's to decide.
7. "Dinner is steady" as rows (`86akh5uaw`, `86akh6748`), before the early morning's gate, which the diagnostic feeds and does not define; the team's contribution is that no node-overload line on the Maitre d's seat is open at the gate.
8. The existential-risk register (`86akh5ubc`), before the first live risk, so that a lead pulled onto one is read as node overload against a register rather than an impression.
9. Who holds an event and where the overnight crew sits (`86akhcz26`, `86akhcz6k`), before either produces a line the inventory can only record as a gap.
10. Session 14's read of a hire that does not hold (`86akhb2w8`), before the first plan closes not held, which is where section 14's hand-off ends.

The one thing on this page a later session cannot revise at ordinary cost: the order of every read, the mode before the person, enforced by the line's form (P4, P8). # S10: Creating the team environment, the playground test, and culture mechanisms

# Session 10: Creating the team environment, as culture mechanisms

Book pp. 304 to 330 (Chapter 4: Creating the team environment: offsites, meetings, and a note on leadership team meetings). Workbook pp. 93 to 97 (Planning and running your offsite; Leadership team snippets and updates). Session task `86ajgmj2u`. Profiles: the People Systems Designer for what the environment is made of and what it may and may not do to a person; the Hospitality Operations Realist for what survives a Friday service, a roster that dissolves at the close, and the pre-service window's real minutes. Canon is cited by version: Canon 1.0 is `brand-guidelines.md`; Deck 3.0 is the brand and experiential guidelines deck. The white paper is "the record" and is cited as WP with its page.

Every position carries one mark: Recommended (the team's position, ready for founder ratification), Founder-gated (requires founder input the team cannot supply), Chef-gated (left open for the chef partner), Team-filled (populated once the team exists). Nothing on this page is landed. Positions restart at P1, instruments at I1, findings at 20.1; readiness rows continue from 119.

Brandon's note on the session task binds the scope: this is where the Playground Philosophy is operationalized or exposed. The brand's stated obligation is to build conditions for agency for customers, founders, and employees. That is a claim. This page turns it into mechanisms, or names which parts of it are, today, a slogan. Her team-environment material is the test instrument. An honest "exposed" is a valid finding on this page, and several of its verdicts are exactly that.

One name collision is held on every sentence. Her "check-ins" and "check-outs" are meeting openers and closers. At Sŏn "the check-in" is the fifteen-minute paid conversation that replaced her 1:1 (S4 P15). On this page "the check-in" always means Sŏn's; her devices are called her meeting opener and her meeting closer, and where any opener or closer survives at Sŏn it carries a different name or none.

* * *

## 1\. Her ask against the record, and how much is already decided

### 1.1 Her ask

Her section opens on a claim: "Rituals and common practices weave the fabric of a team" (Book p.304). What follows is three instruments for weaving it. Offsites: two or three days a year for senior teams, at least one a year for junior ones, planned against the team's development stage on Tuckman's four phases, balanced between task-focused and team-focused activities, opened by a personal check-in, warmed by an icebreaker, structured by purpose, agenda, limit, and notes, and closed by a one-word check-out (Book pp. 304 to 311). Meetings: the team's most frequent activity, costly, only as good as the relationships beneath them, laid on groundwork (common understanding of who is on the team, what each does, how they prefer to work, and agreed norms), given roles (a DRI, a facilitator, a notetaker), owned mutually, given one or two purposes, run to norms (logistics, no undiscussable topics, inclusion, disagree and commit, a parking lot, action items, reconfiguration every three to six months), split between operator mode and creator mode, run with openers and closers, closed by confirming the purpose was achieved, and made decisive by an explicit decision method, a framework, and a decision log (Book pp. 311 to 328). Leadership team meetings: the "first team" a leader commits to above their own reports, Stripe's Monday three hours on snippets and metrics, and a supplemental leadership group for new senior leaders (Book pp. 328 to 330).

Read as one, every instrument assumes a manager who creates the environment by convening people and running the room. The team is made in the meeting; the manager is the maker.

### 1.2 What the record already holds

The record holds a different premise, and it holds most of the ground. The team is a structure, not a meeting: "great nights feel like distributed intelligence rather than coordinated direction... This is not a management achievement. It is the structure functioning correctly" (WP p.8). Culture is named as one of the two phases of the team's material: "The elastic connective tissue is organizational culture: the connective flexibility that allows the structure to flex under stress without fracturing. Culture is not soft. It is the phase that keeps the strong phase from becoming brittle" (WP p.9). Health is bandwidth: "what the system has available after the work of survival is complete... No one has room to feel what is happening, to respond to what is arriving, to improve what is working" (WP p.12), and the order is "Bandwidth, then joy, then retention, then results" (WP p.12; Canon 1.0, section 01; Deck 3.0, p.4). The day already has a rhythm: "Beginning of shift, prepare for the customer. During service, serve them. End of shift, reflect and strengthen the relationship" (WP p.26). Errors are the process's: "the first question is not who failed. It is what allowed this to happen... Management absorbs blame from staff. Post-mortems are private and process-focused" (WP p.17). Employees are the users, with "continuous feedback loops so the tools evolve based on real usage" (WP p.17). Feedback "runs both directions" (WP p.19). Recognition is peer-to-peer "in the moment" (WP p.19). Dignity is physical: a real employee area with secure lockers "is not a perk. It is basic dignity, and dignity is a precondition for presence" (WP p.20). Generosity is pre-authorized: "their judgment is trusted" (WP p.26). And the record's own culture measure names psychological safety directly: "engagement results across psychological safety and values alignment" (WP p.23).

Canon holds the frame. The Playground Philosophy: "The brand's operational obligation across every concept, every daypart, and for customers, founders, and employees, is to build conditions for agency. A playground is a structured space with legible rules and open-ended results. Clear enough to feel safe; open enough to stay" (Canon 1.0, section 01). Its test: "does this build or foreclose conditions for agency? If it forecloses agency without a documented reason, it violates the philosophy" (Canon 1.0, section 01). The deck states the two failure directions: "Rules so tight the result is foreclosed" and "Openness so loose the space stops feeling safe" (Deck 3.0, p.14). The non-negotiables sit above everything executional: "No exploitation ever. No toxicity ever. No disposable people" (Canon 1.0, section 01; Deck 3.0, p.4). Ma forbids "service staff who manufacture activity because standing still feels wrong" and "copy that rushes to fill silence" (Canon 1.0, section 01). Nunchi is "the human expression of the Playground Philosophy at the floor level" and Jeong "cannot be scripted" (Canon 1.0, section 01). The master register is "present without performing" (Canon 1.0, section 01; Deck 3.0, p.27).

### 1.3 What Sessions 1 to 9 already built of a team environment

Nearly everything she asks a manager to convene, an earlier session placed as a mechanism that runs without anyone convening it. The brief and the close with fixed spines, the brief bounding a slot for team content after its operational block (S4 P10, P12). The check-in, fifteen minutes on the clock, with an upward question and a written line read back (S4 P15). The leads' review with a fixed eight-item agenda, a hard stop before the brief, an alternating chair, and notes with owners that are units and never a person below another (S4 P22, P26). The partners' review with a versioned decision log on the partners' page, and the monthly domain read in writing (S4 P53). The house review with memos, a reading block, and a reflection paragraph read at the next opening (S4 P32). The whole-house gathering, founder-gated, conditional, paid, carrying nothing about a person (S4 P38). The mechanism reset as the one place a mechanism is continued, changed, or ended (S4 P39). The four-part entry test and the playground test as gates on any mechanism (S4 P2). The seam protection: no build meeting in the building during service hours, the room's mechanisms frozen for dinner's first quarter (S4 P9). The decision-rights rule in owner, range, triggers form, and its register (S3 4.1, 4.2); the interim two-partner rule argued and held (S3 4.5). The team as the house, with the domain and the service roster as her other two meanings (S8 P6). Per-service designations, never permanent (S8 P22, P24, P25). The mentor from a pool, paid as shift, never scoring (S7 P41, P42). The cohort in two waves, the community her onboarding wanted met by the cohort itself (S7 P8). The career conversation once, in the person's words (S9 P43). The diagnostic reading team state by evidence lines on five objects, never a survey, with the offsite given no diagnostic role (S9 P5, P20, I10). DRIs refused (S9 P38, P39). Blame the process as a founder principle (S1, principle 4). The work style grid out of recruiting, inside working-with-me, with team use left to this page (S5 P8, S7 P53, S8 P40).

What none of them supplied, and what this page does: whether the Playground Philosophy, on the employee side, is a set of mechanisms or a claim; what "conditions for agency" means for a person on the floor, decomposed to conditions that can each be checked against a mechanism; what the brief's team slot carries; whether any offsite exists; what psychological safety is made of here, as the environment's half; what her meeting material does to the mechanisms that already exist; the grid's team use; community after the cohort and the mentor after the plan; the founder side to its ceiling; and the decision rights for all of it.

### 1.4 Where she is refused, and where she is absorbed

Refused as forms: the offsite as the team-forming device; Tuckman's phases as a read of the team; the meeting as the unit in which a team is made; her meeting opener and closer under any name that borrows Sŏn's; the icebreaker; the DRI, the facilitator, and the notetaker as roles; agreed meeting norms as a document per team; the decision-making frameworks and the decision log as a spreadsheet; the personality-types decision exercise; the leadership "first team" as a priority ordering; the supplemental leadership team; the offsite feedback form. Each refusal names what does its work (sections 7, 8, 11, 12, 19).

Absorbed as discipline: her cost-of-meetings arithmetic, which is the bandwidth ledger (S4 10.3); her one-or-two-purposes rule and PAL, which every review on the mechanism map already has as a fixed agenda with a hard stop; her "reconfigure every three to six months," which is the mechanism reset and the quarterly reflection paragraph; "no topics are undiscussable," which at Sŏn is the rule that every topic has a named destination; "the senior person speaks last," which survives whole for a founder in any room; her shared-document benefits (inclusivity, anchoring, pre-work), which are the domain read in writing and the house memo; her observation that psychological safety is what lets a group progress, which this page turns into mechanisms; and her rule that offsites are not for solving talent issues, which the record states from the other side, "before intervening at the people level, identify which failure mode is actually present" (WP p.14).

**P1 (Recommended).** Her environment-by-convening is replaced by environment-by-structure: every condition her offsites and meetings exist to create is assigned to a mechanism that runs without a manager convening it, and her instruments are refused, absorbed, or placed as sections 3 to 12 state. Where a condition has no mechanism, this page says so rather than convening one.

**P2 (Recommended).** This page designs mechanisms and specifications and writes no culture prose. Culture is read from canon and the record and turned into mechanisms; nothing on this page states what Sŏn values beyond what the record and canon already state.

## 2\. The playground test, made operational

### 2.1 What canon states, and what canon specifies

Canon states the obligation three ways and specifies it, in the main, one way. Canon 1.0's Playground section prohibits six things and requires five (Canon 1.0, section 01). Of the eleven, nine are customer-facing: scripted service protocols, spatial routing through a single sequence, menu and brand language that resolves ambiguity, customer data systems that make the customer reconstruct their history, digital interfaces that route, spatial design that holds possibility in reserve, customer history infrastructure, and brand language that names and invites. Two touch the employee: the prohibition on "training systems that measure procedure execution without building toward judgment," and the requirements of "training architecture that progresses from procedure mastery to autonomous judgment" and "service authority distributed to the closest-to-customer position." None touches the founders. The deck adds no list; it states the two failure directions and the requirement of "Conditions for agency for customers, founders, and employees alike" and "Structure legible enough to be trusted, open enough to be inhabited" (Deck 3.0, p.14).

So the employee side of the philosophy arrives at this page with two mechanisms named by canon (a training architecture that reaches judgment, and authority at the edge) and a general obligation. That is the honest starting point for Brandon's question. The philosophy's employee half is neither a slogan nor a system in canon; it is two specified requirements and a claim about everything else.

The tier is held. Canon 1.0 places the Playground Philosophy at tier 2 with positioning and leaves the company non-negotiables unranked; Deck 3.0 places the non-negotiables at tier 2 and the Playground at tier 3 (Canon 1.0, section 02; Deck 3.0, p.32; S2 sections 3 and 4; `86akh3rx4`). Under Deck 3.0 a mechanism that builds agency by breaching a non-negotiable loses; under Canon 1.0 the non-negotiables have no tier to lose from. Every verdict on this page reads the non-negotiables as outranking the philosophy, which is the deck's order, and marks that as held.

### 2.2 The test as a procedure that a mechanism can fail

Canon's test is one question. Run on a mechanism it needs six, so that a mechanism can fail it in a way someone can point to:

1. **The condition.** Which condition for agency the mechanism claims to build, named from the list in 2.3. A mechanism that names none is not a culture mechanism and is tested only by the entry test.
2. **The legible rule.** What the mechanism states in advance, where it is written, and who can read it before acting. A playground's rules are legible or it is not a playground.
3. **The open-ended result.** What the person decides inside the rule, and what the mechanism refuses to decide for them. A rule with no result inside it is a script.
4. **The tight edge.** Does the rule foreclose the result: does it script the act, prescribe the sequence, measure the procedure without the judgment, or let one person's standard stand as the rule? "Rules so tight the result is foreclosed" (Deck 3.0, p.14).
5. **The loose edge.** Does the openness remove the safety: is there an act with no stated limit, a trigger with no destination, a topic with no place to go, a failure with no capture, a night with no one holding the room? "Openness so loose the space stops feeling safe" (Deck 3.0, p.14).
6. **The documented reason, and the read.** Where the mechanism forecloses agency, the reason is written on the mechanism map or the register, because "If it forecloses agency without a documented reason, it violates the philosophy" (Canon 1.0, section 01). And the diagnostic line that would read the condition's absence is named, because a condition no line can read is a condition no one will notice losing.

A mechanism passes when all six are answered and neither edge is crossed. It fails on the tight edge, the loose edge, or a missing reason. It is incomplete when a question cannot be answered from the record, which is a different state from failing and is recorded as such.

### 2.3 What "conditions for agency" means for an employee at Sŏn

The phrase is decomposed here into conditions specific enough that each can be checked against a mechanism. The decomposition is the team's, derived from canon's own definition (legible rules, open-ended results, safe enough, open enough to stay) and the record's people sections, and it is what section 3 tests. Ten conditions:

1. **Legible rules.** The person can read, before acting, what the rules of the seat, the service, and the house are.
2. **A stated range.** The person has authority to act without asking, with its limits and its escalation destinations written in advance.
3. **Judgment built, not procedure only.** The training reaches "autonomous judgment" and something reads whether it did (Canon 1.0, section 01).
4. **Safety to err.** An error is the process's first, captured, and never a verdict on the person.
5. **Safety to speak.** A question, a dissent, a report of a failure, and a concern about a lead each have a destination, and something reads whether they arrive.
6. **Being known.** The house holds the person in their own words, in their own language, and knows what the building must supply for them.
7. **A path.** The next thing is visible before it is asked for, and no one's advancement waits on a manager.
8. **Time that is not taken.** The paid window, the check-in on the clock, the close, and slack exist and are read as bandwidth.
9. **A say in the rules.** What the person reports changes the process, and what the floor reports reaches the rules.
10. **A place of their own.** The physical condition the record names as "a precondition for presence" (WP p.20).

Two things her material wants that are not on the list, and why. "Belonging among the team" is not a condition the philosophy names; canon's "open enough to stay" is the outcome the conditions produce, and the record's order puts retention third, after bandwidth and joy, as an output (WP p.12). Section 14 tests whether the steady state needs a belonging mechanism anyway. "Vulnerability," her fourth interpersonal risk, is not a condition the house builds; a house that asks for it is performing, and canon refuses performing (section 6).

### 2.4 The verdict method

Each condition in section 3 gets one of three verdicts. **Mechanism:** a named mechanism builds it, passes the four-part entry test (bandwidth cost, what it buys, who runs it, where its record lives; S4 P2), passes the six-question test above, and its absence would be read by a diagnostic line that exists. **Partial:** a mechanism builds it for one object and not another (the house but not the roster; the floor but not a lead), or one of the entry test's four parts or the read is missing, or the mechanism exists and cannot yet run because a gated item holds it. **Slogan:** nothing builds it; the philosophy asserts it and no mechanism, existing or specified by an earlier session, produces it; the verdict names what would make it a mechanism and who must decide.

**P3 (Recommended).** The playground test is run on a mechanism as six questions: the condition, the legible rule, the open-ended result, the tight edge, the loose edge, and the documented reason with the read that would notice the condition's absence. Every mechanism on the map is run through it at the reset, and any mechanism proposed after this page is run through it at entry beside the four-part test.

**P4 (Recommended).** "Conditions for agency" for an employee at Sŏn decomposes into ten conditions as listed in 2.3. Each is tested against a mechanism in section 3 and given one of three verdicts: mechanism, partial, or slogan.

**P5 (Recommended).** The non-negotiables outrank the Playground Philosophy on every verdict here, which is Deck 3.0's order; the position is marked as held under `86akh3rx4` because Canon 1.0's hierarchy does not rank them.

## 3\. The conditions, one by one

Each condition: the mechanism that builds it, what it costs, who runs it, where its record lives, how the diagnostic would read its absence, the two edges, and the verdict. Most mechanisms already exist; this page names them as culture mechanisms, which is the thing no earlier page did.

### 3.1 Legible rules

**Mechanism.** The seat sheet, sixteen fields, none blank, "the single account of a seat" read by the candidate before the offer (S5 4.1 to 4.3). The range card, read at orientation, rehearsed, stated at the readiness read (S7 section 12). The non-negotiables, delivered in the why block before operational training, "why comes before how" (WP p.18; S7 P12, P16). The register block per period and the period plan (S7 P30). The team home, "the human-readable face of the operating system," with the decision-rights register, the competency paths, and the standing vocabulary, readable by every team member between services in the team's languages (S3 P11.8). The brief's standing change line, so that "any change to a range, trigger, goal, or mechanism since the last brief" is spoken before it is met (S3 shift brief; S8 P49).

**Cost, runner, record.** Already funded: the sheet and the card are read on paid time; the team home is a build. The domain lead owns the sheet and the card; the Operations Lead holds the register's record; the owner of the room speaks the change line. Records: the sheet's version log, the person page's orientation entry, the team home.

**The read.** Skill invisibility: "employees do not know what advancement requires because the competencies are not documented or accessible" (WP p.14), read by S9 4.6 from blank horizons and unscheduled unlocks; sequence corruption, where a change reached the floor first at the brief or not at all (S9 B2). A rule that exists only in a lead's head is node overload by the ledger's stability rule.

**The edges.** Tight: a sheet or a card that scripts the act rather than bounding it; guarded by the range card's form, which states what the person may and may not do and not how to do it, and by canon's prohibition on "service delivered by script rather than felt knowledge" (Canon 1.0, section 01). Loose: a seat opened without a sheet, which the inventory refuses (S8 P26).

**Verdict: mechanism, with a dependency.** The why block is empty until the charter is ratified (S7 P12), so the rules a person reads first are, today, unwritten; and where the team home lives is founder-gated (S3 P11.9). The mechanism is complete; two gates hold its content.

### 3.2 A stated range

**Mechanism.** The decision-rights rule: "Authority sits with the closest competent owner; the range within which that owner acts without asking is stated in advance; the triggers that escalate are named before the event" (S3 4.1), with canon's floor authority ("server owns the table"), the generosity range ("Every server carries a bottle to gift as they see fit," WP p.26), routine recovery pre-authorized "inside known limits," and escalation triggers "defined before service, not improvised at the table" (Canon 1.0, section 08; Deck 3.0, p.79). The range travels with the offer as a sheet field (S5 P12, field 10) and is on the range card.

**Cost, runner, record.** None beyond the register's upkeep; the domain lead sets ranges one level out; the register on the team home; every use of the range is captured in the close and reviewed by the lead, "a capture trigger rather than an escalation trigger" (S3 4.2, instance 8).

**The read.** Under-use: "the range is to be used, and under-use is the failure the record names" (S3 4.2, instance 8); the close's range-use count by section is a tension-slack source (S9 P9) and this page reads a range unused across a quarter as the tight edge on the person's seat. Over-escalation: calls deferred to a lead inside the server's range are a node-overload signal on the lead (S9 P10). A trigger with no destination is a structural hole (S3 4.1, rule 1).

**The edges.** Tight: a lead who "backs up without intercepting" (Canon 1.0, section 08) and intercepts; the check-in's "what is in the way" aggregated by friction is where that surfaces, never by the person's name (S9 4.7). Loose: a range with no "may not" (S3 4.1, rule 2).

**Verdict: mechanism, incomplete on values.** The rule and the register exist; the threshold's value and the "known limits" are unwritten and set with Dominic's domain at S13 (S3 4.2, instances 3 and 8). Until then the card "states the hold in words" (S7 section 3), which is a legible rule with an open number inside it. A pre-opening cohort will be trained on a range whose money edge is a sentence, and the Realist's read is that on a Friday a sentence holds better than a number no one has rehearsed, but not for a whole quarter.

### 3.3 Judgment built, not procedure only

**Mechanism.** Canon's own requirement, "training architecture that progresses from procedure mastery to autonomous judgment" (Canon 1.0, section 01). The training sequence: modules, live session, observed service, paired services, readiness read, then solo (S6 P38; S7 P10). The readiness form with language, range, and felt-knowledge rows beyond the practical's procedure rows (S7 I7). The felt-knowledge block, canon's "service speaks to a dish with felt knowledge, not recited description" (Canon 1.0, section 01; S7 section 9). The step-back architecture, "attunement-triggered, not timer-triggered" (Canon 1.0, section 08), which is a service model that cannot be executed by procedure at all. And the invisible advocate, which unlocks the next skill set without a manager (WP p.11).

**Cost, runner, record.** Paid training time, already funded; the assessor from the pool scores, the domain lead records (S8 P37); the readiness form and the fluency record on the person page.

**The read.** S9 finding 19.7: the record's skill-invisibility fix is documentation and canon's test is judgment; S9 4.6 added canon's test to the mode's read. After readiness, the only reads of judgment are the close's range-use count (a judgment exercised) and the captures resolved inside range (a judgment that held). No line reads whether judgment grew in a person after the form, and the four scorecard dimensions read "self-directed mastery" from the advocate's own record (S6 P33), which is preparation and not judgment.

**The edges.** Tight: a module that measures procedure execution only; the readiness form's range row is the guard, and the module standard (`86akhb2kk`) must carry canon's requirement as a row. Loose: a person on the floor before the form reads ready, which the record forbids in words (WP p.19) and `86akhb2k5` holds one reading of.

**Verdict: partial.** The architecture reaches judgment by construction and the form reads it once. Nothing reads it after, except by inference from range use. What would make it a mechanism: the module standard carrying canon's judgment requirement as a row a module fails, and the reset reading range use per seat as a judgment count. Who decides: the module standard's approver (S7 finding 19.1, `86akhb2kk`) and the reset. Recommended in section 19 as I6's environment reads.

### 3.4 Safety to err

**Mechanism.** Blame the process: "when something goes wrong, the first question is not who failed. It is what allowed this to happen... Management absorbs blame from staff. Post-mortems are private and process-focused. The system gets fixed so it does not happen again, to anyone" (WP p.17). The capture at the close, "the system captures the incident in the shift close, the appropriate lead reviews, the process that allowed the failure gets updated" (WP p.13), in less time than the thank-you note (S4 P12). The close carries nothing about a person and no post-mortem (S4 P12). The person page carries no verdict, no rating, no free text about the person (S7 P25 to P29). The check-in refuses verdicts and discipline (S4 P15). The evidence line names no person (S9 P8). The one path a read reaches a person is tension slack, last (S9 P41). Principle 4 applies it to the founders' own domains first (S1).

**Cost, runner, record.** The capture's seconds at the close, a stack failure if longer than the note; the person who held the table captures, the reviewing lead updates, the post-mortem is that lead's off the floor; the capture log, the process's version.

**The read.** The capture rate and the process-update rate are item 1 of the leads' review every week (S4 P26), and S9 placed the capture rate and the error-reporting rate as the diagnostic's safety source (S9 3.3). A capture written by a lead on behalf of the floor is sequence corruption (S9 3.3); a falling capture rate on a rising incident count is the loose edge of safety read as a count.

**The edges.** Tight: a capture form that asks who; the close's spine refuses it. Loose: a failure that is genuinely a person's (a non-negotiable breached) treated as the process's; the non-negotiable flag goes to both leads the same day (S7 P45), which is the one case the record treats as a person's, and section 6 places what the environment does with it.

**Verdict: mechanism.** The most complete condition on the page, because the record wrote it as mechanics and Sessions 3 to 9 refused every verdict-shaped instrument that would have undone it. The response by type of failure (basic, complex, intelligent) is S12's, and the page states that dependency in section 6.

### 3.5 Safety to speak

**Mechanism.** Four speech acts, each with a destination. A question: the mentor, "the person a new hire asks before they ask the lead" (S7 P42), and the check-in's "what is in the way" (S4 P15). A dissent: the joint half-page as the form of a Class B or C hold, with the refusal to hear a unilateral case (S8 P50), and the check-in's upward question in the person's own words. A report of a failure: the capture (3.4). A concern about the house or a lead: the check-in's fourth question, "the person's read on the lead and the house" (S4 P15), and the feedback channel, "a dedicated channel that syncs to the execution system, so employees can surface issues, suggest improvements, and see their input lead to action. Feedback without follow-through breeds cynicism. The loop gets closed" (WP p.22), with seven days to acknowledge and thirty to close (S4 P30). The pulse, one anonymous question, monthly (S4 P29). The non-negotiable flag to both leads (S7 P45).

**Cost, runner, record.** The check-in's minute, the channel's entry; the lead of the person's domain, the item's owner, the Maitre d for the pulse; the person page's line, the channel's items and their state, the pulse composite.

**The read.** Item 5 of the leads' review, items open past the loop-closure window (S4 P26); feedback items past thirty days as a cooling-failure source (S9 P13); the count of check-in lines under "what is in the way," aggregated by friction. The record's own words: "the best ideas and the earliest warnings both come from the people doing the work" (WP p.19).

**The edges.** Tight: a check-in whose line is written in the lead's words; the read-back rule guards it (S4 P15). Loose, and this is where the condition is not whole: a concern about the lead who holds the check-in has, today, one destination that the lead does not hold, the anonymous pulse, which is one question and reads no content; the feedback channel's item goes to "the lead or unit the item names," which for a lead is that lead. S9 finding 19.9 named it: upward feedback has no reader beyond the lead, and who holds a lead's check-in is open (`86akhb2jg`). Until it closes, the fourth speech act reaches the lead about the lead and nowhere else with content.

**Verdict: partial.** Three of four speech acts are mechanisms. The fourth is a mechanism for the house and a slogan for the lead until `86akhb2jg` closes: the record commits "Team members weigh in on management effectiveness" (WP p.19) and builds no reader for it above the lead. What would make it a mechanism: the lead's check-in holder ruled, so that a floor person's concern about a lead has a named destination that is not the lead, delivered through the channel's routing rule. Who decides: the founders, `86akhb2jg`, already urgent in the ledger; this page adds the environment's reason to the urgency.

### 3.6 Being known

**Mechanism.** The person page, written only at the check-in, read back, readable by the person at any time, in the person's words (S4 P18; S7 P25 to P29). The check-in on a fixed interval placed by the stack, so that the house asks rather than waits (S4 P15). The fourth read at hiring, "what the building must supply for this person to succeed" (S5 3.1; WP p.18), carried onto the person page as the baseline. The interview in the candidate's language, "Language choice protects dignity" (WP p.17), and the brief "spoken in the languages the team speaks" (S4 P10). The mentor matched for language and overlap (S7 P41). The career conversation, once, opening on the person's own path line (S9 P43). The peer recognition platform, read aloud at the brief (WP p.19; S4 P10, item 4).

**Cost, runner, record.** The check-in's fifteen minutes; the lead of the domain; the person page.

**The read.** The person page's "what the building must supply" unsupplied is a training-infrastructure line (S7 I16); a check-in moved twice is a load reading, three times a node-overload entry (S4 P20); a person page with no line in the person's words in an interval is sequence corruption on the check-in.

**The edges.** Tight: a page that accumulates a lead's or a mentor's account of the person; refused (S7 P42; S4 P18). Loose: being known only by a system, which the record itself names as the failure on the customer side, "being known by someone, not just recognized by a system" (WP p.25).

**Verdict: partial.** By the house, through the lead, the condition is a mechanism, and it is a stronger one than her groundwork of "who's on the team, what each person's role is, and how they prefer to work" (Book p.313), because it is in the person's words and on the clock. Among the team, it is thin: the roster changes every service, the mentor is the one peer relationship the house places, and recognition is the one peer voice the house carries. The record wrote "being known" in full for the customer (WP pp. 25 to 26) and for the team wrote a break space. Section 14 tests whether the steady state needs more; the verdict here is that the house knows the person and the team knows the person only as much as the schedule and the mentor produce.

### 3.7 A path

**Mechanism.** "The path is explicit before they start it. Every position has documented competency requirements visible to anyone. Employees do not need to ask what it takes to advance. They open the system and see it" (WP p.11). The invisible advocate: "After a set period in any role, the next skill set unlocks automatically. It is self-paced... No one's advancement waits on a manager's attention or judgment. The system is the advocate" (WP p.11). Tracks visible from day one including another domain's (S7 P39). Advancement as three seats: the stack schedules, an assessor scores, the lead records and may not override (S8 P37). The fluency record (S8 P35). The career conversation writing one track in the person's words (S9 P43). No levels, no ladders (S8 P30).

**Cost, runner, record.** The platform and the forms; the stack; the person page and the pool.

**The read.** Skill invisibility, the record's own mode, read by S9 4.6 from blank horizons, unlocks that did not auto-schedule or were overridden, and an empty pool at a departure.

**The edges.** Tight: a lead who "assigns work to develop someone" (S9 13.5, refused). Loose: a path with no unlock period on the sheet, which the sheet's field 6 refuses to leave blank.

**Verdict: mechanism, gated on the platform existing.** The record's most complete employee condition, and canon's "advancement requires preparation, not permission" (WP p.14) is the philosophy's plainest employee sentence. It cannot run until the learning platform and the first module set exist (S7 P9), and its wording is held between two accounts (`86akhcz22`). The mechanism is whole; the building is not built.

### 3.8 Time that is not taken

**Mechanism.** The pre-service window as paid time and "the highest-leverage time a restaurant has" (S4 4.3). The check-in as the first fifteen minutes of a scheduled shift, never mid-service, never at the close (S4 P15). The close window protected for the note and the capture, with cleaning moved to the overnight crew (WP p.26; S4 P12). The bandwidth ledger, which prices every mechanism in time per person and argues the total as lower than hers for the hourly team: "no weekly team meeting beyond the brief, no biweekly 1:1, no monthly all-hands, no daily standup separate from the brief" (S4 10.3). The seam protection: no build meeting during service hours (S4 P9). Slack as a system property, which the record commits as the cooling system (WP pp. 16 to 17) and the Realist tests as "is anyone free at 8:15." Nothing required before the first paid hour (S7 P15).

**Cost, runner, record.** This condition is the cost column itself; the stack's schedule; the schedule, the closes' thermal-load lines, the pulse.

**The read.** Cooling failure, read by S9 P13 from the pulse composite, the thermal-load lines, the bandwidth flag on goals, tension-loss departures, aggregated friction lines, feedback items past thirty days, and seam breaches. This page adds two environment-side sources in section 15: a brief whose team slot is dropped every night, and a close whose note displaced the capture.

**The edges.** Tight: a window so full that the check-in is moved twice; the load triggers guard it (S4 P20). Loose: a labor model with no slack, which "looks identical" to a lean one "on a calm night" (Realist profile) and is a figure this program does not hold.

**Verdict: partial.** The mechanisms exist and the reads exist. Three things keep it from whole: the close window's length is unstated in the record (S4 findings; ledger open question), so "time not taken" at the close cannot be checked against a stated allocation; the cultural labor score is undefined (`86akh5u9x`), so the pulse's one question is the only defined read of how the team is doing; and slack is a labor figure the program cannot see. What would make it a mechanism: the window's length stated as a reset parameter, the score defined, and the labor model read for slack with Dominic's domain. Who decides: the founders and the Realist's read at the first reset.

### 3.9 A say in the rules

**Mechanism.** On the process, daily: the capture updates the process nightly, "the next server inherits a system that has already learned from it" (WP p.13), logged as care (S9 P24). On the tools: "Employees are the users... continuous feedback loops so the tools evolve based on real usage" (WP p.17), the feedback channel syncing to the execution system, and Class E's rule that no stack change altering what a server does lands without the affected domain consulted (S3 4.3). On the rules: the mechanism reset reads "every mechanism's record, cost, buy" (S4 P39) and the principles revision reads "principles against moments actually had" (S4 10.2); both read records the floor wrote, the captures, the closes, the channel, the check-in lines.

**Cost, runner, record.** None beyond the channel's entry; the reviewing lead for care, the reset for correction; the capture log, the channel, the reset's record.

**The read.** The process-update rate (S4 P26, item 1); channel items closed as a rate; "Feedback without follow-through breeds cynicism" (WP p.22) is read as items past thirty days.

**The edges.** Tight: a rule changed only at the reset when a capture could have changed it nightly; the care-or-correction line guards it (S9 P24). Loose: a floor that changes the process by habit rather than capture, which is drift by the deck's word (Deck 3.0, p.94).

**Verdict: partial.** The say in the process is a mechanism and it is the record's best-built loop. The say in the rules is indirect: the reset is "the center with the leads" (S4 10.2), the house review's memos are the leads' and the center's, and no floor voice is in either room; the floor's records are read, the floor is not asked. The whole-house gathering, if approved, is the one room the floor is in, and section 9 gives its team-making half one item that makes this a mechanism: an open question from the reset put to the house with the channel as its destination. What would make it a mechanism: that item, or a standing reset agenda item drawn from the channel's most-raised items of the year. Who decides: the founders, with the gathering (`86akh5uc7`, `86akh673u`) and the reset's agenda.

### 3.10 A place of their own

**Mechanism.** The record's: "Smart lockers for every team member... A real employee area with secure lockers and a comfortable break space is not a perk. It is basic dignity, and dignity is a precondition for presence" (WP pp. 19 to 20). "If it matters, Sŏn pays for it. Employees should not subsidize it" (WP p.19). The locker assigned before arrival (WP p.18).

**Cost, runner, record.** A build cost this program does not price; the Operations Lead for facility integrity (WP p.10); the surface-and-zone baseline document, which "lives in ClickUp doc 2ky45bmy-15773" (Canon 1.0, section 01), archived and excluded (`86akh3tp5`).

**The read.** None. No diagnostic line reads whether the employee area exists, because no session has needed one: a first-shift walk depends on it (S7 finding 19.11) and readiness rows for onboarding assume it.

**The edges.** Not applicable; the condition is physical.

**Verdict: slogan today.** The record promises it, canon's nine-beat spatial sequence does not place it, canon's pre-CD open items do not list it, and the baseline document that would hold it is unreachable (S7 finding 19.11; `86akhb2kb`). It is the cleanest "exposed" on this page: a condition the record calls a precondition for presence, with no zone, no drawing, and no row. What would make it a mechanism: a zone in the surface-and-zone baseline with its aging intention like every other surface, and a readiness row that a first shift's walk can pass. Who decides: the founders with canon's owner, `86akhb2kb`, before the first cohort's first shift.

### 3.11 The table

| Condition | Mechanism | Runner | Record | Read of absence | Verdict |
| ---| ---| ---| ---| ---| --- |
| Legible rules | Sheet, range card, why block, team home, change line | Domain lead; owner of the room | Sheet log, person page, team home | Skill invisibility; sequence corruption | Mechanism; why block and team home gated |
| A stated range | Register, floor authority, generosity range | Domain lead, one level out | Register; close's captures | Range unused; calls deferred; trigger with no destination | Mechanism; values open (S13) |
| Judgment built | Training sequence, readiness form, felt knowledge, step-back | Assessor, lead records | Person page | Range use as a count; S9 19.7 | Partial |
| Safety to err | Blame the process, the capture, no verdicts | Table holder; reviewing lead | Capture log | Capture rate falling | Mechanism |

**P6 (Recommended).** The ten conditions are built as tabled: four mechanisms (legible rules, a stated range, safety to err, a path), five partial (judgment, safety to speak, being known, time not taken, a say in the rules), and one slogan (a place of their own). Each partial names the decision that would complete it; the slogan names the zone and the row that would make it a mechanism.

**P7 (Recommended).** Two things her material wants are not conditions the house builds directly: belonging among the team, which is the outcome the conditions produce and section 14 tests for a steady-state mechanism, and vulnerability, which the house does not ask for.

## 4\. Designed autonomy against drift, both ways

Brandon's gloss on the session task, designed autonomy rather than freedom, is not canon's wording and is not quoted here as canon. What canon states is the two edges (Deck 3.0, p.14). This section asks what holds each edge over time, because a playground is not built once; it drifts, and the drift has a direction on each side.

### 4.1 The tight edge: rules tightening until the result is foreclosed

Three drifts the Realist expects on a real floor, and what holds each.

**Scripted service.** The rush's first instinct is a script, because a script is reproducible by a green crew. Canon forbids it three times: "service protocols built entirely on scripted delivery" (Playground), "service delivered by script rather than felt knowledge" (Mahk), and Jeong "cannot be scripted into the opening of a service interaction" (Canon 1.0, section 01). What holds it: the step-back architecture's trigger is attunement and cannot be scripted (Canon 1.0, section 08); the readiness form's felt-knowledge rows read for it (S7 I7); the brief's spine carries no script and refuses any item that is one (S4 13.1); and the reset reads the close's range-use count, so a section whose range is never used across a quarter is read as the tight edge on that seat, not as a well-run section (section 3.2). The one scripted line canon itself fixes, "We have you" at the threshold (Canon 1.0, section 08), is a legible rule with an open result behind it, which is the difference.

**Procedure-only training.** A module that measures procedure and stops is the drift canon names at tier 1 or 2 depending on the version. What holds it: the module standard must carry canon's judgment requirement as a row (section 3.3; `86akhb2kk`); the readiness form's range row; and the invisible advocate, which unlocks the next set on a period and not on a manager's judgment that the person is "ready for more," which is where procedure-only training usually hides.

**A lead's personal standard becoming the rule.** This is the drift the record is least defended against, because the Maitre d owns "Service culture and the emotional standard of the room" (WP p.10) and no versioned document holds what that standard is beyond canon's service model. A lead who says at the brief "here is how I want it done tonight" has made a rule with no version, no register entry, and no reason. What holds it: the brief refuses any item that changes a range, trigger, or mechanism except through the standing change line, which reads a versioned change and never announces one (S8 P49); a rule not on the register, a sheet, a module, or canon is not a rule, and a check-in line naming "the lead's way" as what is in the way is aggregated as a friction and read at the leads' review (S9 P13); the change record refuses a change with no reason line (S9 P25); and the readiness row S8 wrote that no change reaches the team by announcement (S8 P49, row 102). What does not hold it: the record's "emotional standard of the room" has no owner above the Maitre d but canon, and canon's owner is held (`86akh3t3y`). Section 20 records the silence.

### 4.2 The loose edge: openness loosening until the space stops feeling safe

**An act with no limit.** The range's "may not" (S3 4.1, rule 2). The financial threshold and the known limits, unset today (S3 4.2), are the one place the loose edge is open by the record's own gap: a server told "use your judgment" with no number is not free, they are unprotected, because the first recovery above a limit no one stated is a conversation about the person. The Realist's read: until the value is set, the card's sentence is the limit, and the lead's review of every capture is the guard.

**A night with no one holding the room.** The room designation on every service the Maitre d does not work (S8 P25), the door and sequence designations, and the pass owned (S8 P22, P23). "Unowned, the line buries itself" (Realist profile).

**A topic with no place to go.** Every trigger names a destination (S3 4.1, rule 1); the non-negotiable flag to both leads (S7 P45); the feedback channel's loop. Section 6 answers "no topics are undiscussable" from this side.

**A failure with no capture.** The close's capture, and the capture rate read weekly.

**A person with no rules to stand on.** The non-negotiables held whole and delivered first: "No Toxicity Ever" is the loose edge's floor, and it is above the Playground in the deck's order (section 2.1). A house whose openness reached a toxic act and called it agency would have violated the tier above.

**Where the record is silent.** What happens when a range is used badly, not above its limit but inside it and wrong, is not in the record; it is S12's (feedback) and S14's (performers), and this page states the dependency. And what the environment does with the first quarter, when every rule is new and the freeze forbids changing any of them (S4 P9), is answered by the freeze itself: the loose edge is guarded in the first quarter by the rules not moving, and the tight edge by the reset being the only place they can.

**P8 (Recommended).** The tight edge is held by the step-back trigger, the felt-knowledge and range rows on the readiness form, the module standard carrying canon's judgment requirement, the brief's refusal of any unversioned rule, the change record's reason line, and the reset reading range use as a count. The loose edge is held by the range's "may not," the designations on every service, the trigger-with-destination rule, the capture, and the non-negotiables above the philosophy. A lead's personal standard becoming the rule is the tight-edge drift the record is least defended against, and the guard is that a rule with no version is not a rule.

**P9 (Recommended).** Inside dinner's first quarter the freeze is the environment's own guard: the loose edge is held by the rules not moving, the tight edge by the reset being the only place they can move. No culture mechanism starts inside the freeze; it is in place before dinner opens or waits for the first reset.

## 5\. The team that forms and dissolves every service

### 5.1 Her stages, and the three objects they would have to describe

Tuckman's forming, storming, norming, performing (Book pp. 306 to 308, Table 7) describes a fixed group of people meeting repeatedly over time, with a manager who is directive in forming and consultative by norming. Her guidance follows the stage: build safety and norms while forming, frame conflict as healthy while storming, celebrate and hone while norming, raise the rate of challenge while performing, and "know that this phase is not permanent" (Book p.307).

Sŏn has one team in her sense, the house, and her word means three things (S8 P6). Her stages have to be tested against each, and each gives a different answer.

**The service roster.** The people the brief named for one service, across every domain; it exists for one service and dissolves at the close (S8 3.2). It cannot form, storm, or norm as a group, because it does not meet again as that group. The Realist's read is exact: a roster has to perform on its first service, so every stage before performing has to be done before the roster exists, by the structure the roster instantiates. Forming is the brief: the designations named (who holds the room, the door, the sequence, the pass), the readiness block, the period's goal, the one thing, and the roster is formed in the time it takes to say them (S4 P10; S8 section 8). Storming is refused as a stage the roster is allowed: its conflicts are resolved by the register before the service (the pass owner and the sequence designation's rule for a station down, S8 P23; the live cross-domain call, S4 P61), and a conflict the register did not anticipate is a capture at the close and a hold at the leads' review, not a stage the roster works through. Norming happened once, for the house, and the roster inherits it. Performing is the record's own picture of a great night, "every element in relationship with every other, information moving laterally without routing through a chain of command" (WP p.8), and it is produced by the structure or not at all.

**The house.** The one team forms once, pre-opening, through the cohort in two waves and the training services (S7 P8, P10). It storms, if the word is kept, in dinner's first quarter, which is exactly why the freeze exists: the record's own quarter "so the heart is solid before anything is added to it" (WP p.36) is her storming phase with a rule that the norms do not move while it runs. It norms at the first mechanism reset, where every mechanism is continued, changed, or ended on the quarter's record (S4 P39; S9 6.1), which is the one time the house's rules are re-set on evidence rather than assertion. Its performing has no stage; the record's health state, "an active positive condition where every system functions and the whole operates with bandwidth" (WP p.12), is what the diagnostic reads for, quarterly, on five modes, and "this phase is not permanent" is the reset's own premise.

**The cohort.** Her forming guidance is the training sequence's own shape and needs no translation: "be more directive," "provide extra support, direction, and modeling in activities," "actively work to build psychological safety by setting up collaborative, supportive team norms" (Table 7) are the modules, the live session, the observed and paired services with the mentor, the why block delivering the non-negotiables first, and the readiness read (S7 P10; S6 P38). The cohort forms in training services and its first solos are held there, so that no one's first solo is dinner's first service (S7 P10). Her suggestion that forming is "a great time to conduct one of the work style and personality preference exercises" (Book p.308) is refused; the grid does not enter onboarding or the cohort (S7 P53; section 13).

**The domain.** A domain is not a team (S8 P6) and does not form; its people meet their lead one at a time at the check-in and each other on the roster.

### 5.2 Task against team, her Table 8

Her offsite balances task-focused activities (metrics, goals and DRIs, retrospectives, long-term strategy) against team-focused ones (work style activity, a meal together, defining norms, discussing roles and accountability) (Book pp. 308 to 309, Table 8). At Sŏn every task-focused item is already on the mechanism map at a fixed rhythm: metrics at the leads' review weekly and the house review quarterly; goals at the house review; retrospectives as the reflection paragraph and the reset; long-term strategy as the gate review and the partners' domain read (S4 10.2). Her team-focused items land as follows. Defining team norms: refused as an act a team performs; the norms are the non-negotiables, the register, and the spines, written once and versioned, never agreed per group (section 8). Discussing roles and accountability: the designation block at the brief, nightly, in one line each. The work style activity: refused (section 13). Team building as an activity: refused as a manufactured activity under Ma (Canon 1.0, section 01). A meal together: the one item on her list the record and canon are silent on, and the silence is the environment's most consequential (5.3).

### 5.3 The staff meal, a silence the brief did not anticipate

Her table's "team breakfast, lunch, dinner activity" is, in a restaurant, the staff meal before service: the one team mechanism the industry already runs daily, at no meeting cost, in the paid pre-service window, and the one place a roster eats together before it serves together. Neither the white paper nor either canon artifact mentions it. The record allocates the pre-service window to "prepare for the customer" (WP p.26) and the brief, and canon's pre-service scene is a lighting and sonic program "30 to 45 minute... before first seating" (Canon 1.0, section 06). Whether the window carries a meal, who cooks it, and what it costs the kitchen's mise are not in the record.

The team does not invent Sŏn's intent here and does not recommend a meal as a culture mechanism from scratch. It records the silence as a founder decision with a chef-gated half, because the meal is the one team-focused item on her list that passes the entry test on its face: it costs no meeting, it buys the roster ten minutes together that "time not taken" already funds, its runner is the kitchen, and its record is none. The Realist's constraint is stated with it: a meal that sits inside the mise window on a Friday is a station's cost, and the chef confirms whether the kitchen can carry it; a meal that displaces the brief is refused. Whether Sŏn holds one is the founders' with the chef.

**P10 (Recommended).** Her development stages are refused as a read of any team and absorbed as three shapes: the service roster is formed by the brief in the time it takes to name the designations and performs or does not on its first service; the house forms once through the cohort, holds its rules still through dinner's first quarter, and re-sets them at the first reset; the cohort forms through the training sequence, whose shape is her forming guidance already. A domain does not form.

**P11 (Recommended).** Her task-focused activities are the mechanism map's fixed rhythms. Her team-focused activities are refused (norms agreed per team, the work style activity, team building as an activity) or placed (roles as the designation block at the brief), except the meal, which the record does not hold.

**P12 (Founder-gated).** Whether the pre-service window carries a staff meal, as the one team mechanism on her list the record is silent on and the one that passes the entry test on its face. The team states the silence and the Realist's constraint, and recommends nothing from scratch.

**P13 (Chef-gated).** The kitchen's cost of a staff meal inside the mise window, if the founders open the question.
