## 6\. Psychological safety, the environment's half

### 6.1 Her definition, placed act by act

Her definition, from Project Aristotle, is "the ability to take interpersonal risks like asking questions, offering a dissenting opinion, discussing a failure, or expressing vulnerability without fear of negative repercussions," which she calls "a central requirement for teams to progress from one phase to the next" (Book p.306). Session 9 placed the signal (the capture rate, the error-reporting rate) as a source the diagnostic reads and handed the system that produces candor to Session 12 (S9 3.3). This page places the environment's half: what makes each of her four acts safe by construction, before any coaching or feedback conversation exists.

**Asking a question.** The mentor, who "answers questions" (WP p.18) and is "the person a new hire asks before they ask the lead" (S7 P42); the check-in's "what is in the way"; the feedback channel. Safe because none of the three writes anything about the asker: the mentor writes nothing on the person page, the check-in's line is the person's own, and the channel's item names a friction.

**Offering a dissenting opinion.** The joint half-page as the form of a hold, with a lead's refusal to hear a unilateral case (S8 P50); the check-in's upward question; the dissent line in the hiring packet (S6 section 19). Safe because a dissent at Sŏn is a written entry on a record with a named destination, not a thing said in a room to a person who decides; and because the decision-rights rule means the dissenter is never asking someone above them to change their mind, only asking the owner to consult, which the owner must do before the event under Class B (S3 4.3).

**Discussing a failure.** The capture and blame the process (section 3.4). Safe because the post-mortem is "private and process-focused" (WP p.17) and "Management absorbs blame from staff" (WP p.17), and because the close carries nothing about a person.

**Expressing vulnerability.** Refused as a mechanism. The house does not ask, and no opener, prompt, or ritual invites it: a person brings what they bring to the check-in and it is written only if they say it and only in their words. Canon's register is "present without performing" (Canon 1.0, section 01), her personal check-in example (a parent's surgery, apologies for distraction, Book p.309) is precisely a performed vulnerability, and the non-negotiables' refusal of intrusion (S9 P44, on the career conversation's origin questions) applies. What the house offers instead is the thing the record names: "dignity is a precondition for presence" (WP p.20), which is a locker and a break space, not a prompt.

### 6.2 What safety is made of here

Six things, all mechanisms already on the map: blame the process (WP p.17); the capture at the close (WP p.13; S4 P12); private, process-focused post-mortems off the floor (WP p.17; S4 P12); the check-in's refusals of verdicts, task assignment, pay, and discipline (S4 P15); nothing on a person page but states and the person's own words (S7 P25 to P29); and the non-negotiables above the philosophy (section 2.1). A seventh is the range: a pre-authorized act is not an interpersonal risk, "pre-authorizing it signals trust to staff" (WP p.26), so the range itself is a safety mechanism, and the size of the range is the size of what a person can do without fear.

What the environment does not supply, and states as dependencies. The response by type of failure (basic, complex, intelligent), which decides whether a capture is met with a process fix or something else, is S12's. What happens when a non-negotiable is breached by a person, the one failure the record treats as a person's, is S14's and S15's; the environment's rule is only that the flag goes to both leads the same day (S7 P45) and that it is never said at the brief or the close.

### 6.3 The measure, and a finding

The record commits "engagement results across psychological safety and values alignment" as a cultural measure (WP p.23). That is a survey-shaped measure, and Session 9 refused the survey as a form (S9 P5, I10). The record's own measure of safety therefore has no instrument the program accepts. What stands in: the capture rate and the process-update rate, on item 1 of the leads' review every week (S4 P26), and the error-reporting rate the designer's seat instruments (S9 3.3); the pulse's one question; and check-in lines aggregated by friction. A baseline for all three is team-filled from the first quarter. Section 20 records the finding.

### 6.4 "No topics are undiscussable," and correcting bad meeting behavior

Her norm is that a team agrees to bring lurking issues to the table because it will smell them eventually, and she calls it the meeting form of "Say the thing you think you cannot say" (Book pp. 317 to 318). At Sŏn the rule is inverted and stronger: every topic has a named destination, and the undiscussable topic is the one with no destination, which is the trigger with no destination the ledger forbids (S3 4.1, rule 1). A friction goes to the check-in or the channel; a dissent to the hold; a failure to the capture; a non-negotiable to both leads; a lead's own concern to the leads' review as a Class B or C entry; a founder's to the partners' page. Her "stinky fish" as a periodic reminder is the leads' review's item 5, items open past the window, read every week whether or not anyone remembers them (S4 P26). What the environment cannot yet route is a concern about a lead that the lead does not hold (section 3.5), and that is the one undiscussable topic left in the house until `86akhb2jg` closes.

Her "correct bad meeting behavior" has two halves. Inside the room: her rule that it is fair to call out a violated norm in a nonjudgmental way (Book p.327). At Sŏn the correction inside a meeting-shaped mechanism is the spine, not a person: the chair holds the clock and declines an item off the agenda (S4 P27); the owner of the room runs the brief's spine and takes no item about a person (S4 13.1); a Class B case argued unilaterally is refused until written jointly (S8 P50). No one is corrected in front of the roster, ever, because the brief and the close carry nothing about a person. Outside the room: her rule that behavior is corrected privately and quickly (Book p.328) is the check-in's own placement, and its content is S12's. Her example of naming someone's work style in a leadership meeting ("acting a bit 'red'") is refused whole: the grid is never spoken about another person (section 13). Her "praise publicly" is the peer recognition read aloud at the brief, "not editorialized" (S4 P10); "criticize privately" is the check-in and nowhere else.

**P14 (Recommended).** Psychological safety's environment half is made of blame the process, the capture, private process-focused post-mortems, the check-in's refusals, a person page with no verdict, the non-negotiables above the philosophy, and the range as a pre-authorized act. Her four acts are placed: a question to the mentor, the check-in, or the channel; a dissent to the hold's joint half-page or the upward question; a failure to the capture; vulnerability refused as a mechanism. The response by failure type is S12's; a non-negotiable breach by a person is S14's and S15's.

**P15 (Recommended).** "No topics are undiscussable" is the rule that every topic has a named destination, and the one undiscussable topic left is a concern about a lead that the lead holds, until `86akhb2jg` closes. Bad behavior in a meeting-shaped mechanism is corrected by the spine and the chair's clock, never by naming a person in the room; the private correction is the check-in's and S12's; the work style call-out is refused.

**P16 (Team-filled).** The safety baseline from the first quarter: the capture rate, the process-update rate, and the pulse composite, written at the first house review.

## 7\. Offsites

### 7.1 Whether Sŏn holds any

Her offsite has three objectives: "Evolve a set of people from a work group into a team. Evaluate progress and determine near-term priorities and goals. Engender long-term strategic thinking" (Book p.305). Each is tested for the three groups an offsite could gather.

**The house.** Refused. A whole-house offsite costs a closed service, which is the whole-house gathering's cost and is already founder-gated (S3 P11.7; S4 P38); a second closed day for a second gathering would be a second cost with no read the diagnostic accepts, because team state is read by the evidence line and never by an offsite (S9 P5; `86akhpvhj`). Her first objective is met for the house by the cohort and the training services (section 5); her second by the house review; her third is the partners' and not the house's.

**The leads.** Refused as a separate event. The leads are two people and the kitchen's seat, they meet weekly with a hard stop (S4 P22), they meet the partners monthly in the check-in's form (S4 P59), and the first two leads' onboarding is "the partners' review from arrival, the pre-reads, and each other" (S7 P25). Her leadership offsite's "step back, evaluate the business, and jointly make decisions to evolve the company" (Book p.304) is, for the leads, the mechanism reset, where they sit with the center and every mechanism is read on its record (S4 P39).

**The partners.** The reset and the principles revision are the two annual points where the partners do exactly what her offsite does, and both sit at a closed hour outside service hours by the seam rule (S4 P9, P58). The team recommends that the two be held as one closed-hour block per year, and that whether the partners hold it away from the building is theirs and costs the room nothing. That is her offsite reduced to its decision content: the reset's agenda (every mechanism's record, cost, and buy; the Maitre d's seat read first, S9 P36) and the revision's ("principles against moments actually had," S4 10.2), with the working-with-me documents on the table as the gate review already has them (S4 P53). No figure is stated for the partners' time; none is needed, because the block replaces nothing and adds no service cost. Her "creator mode" offsite, "multi-hour 'creator' meetings held every four to six weeks" (Book p.319), is pre-opening's build itself, weekly at the partners' review (S4 9.2), and in service the annual block; section 10 holds the rest.

**The cohort.** The one thing at Sŏn that resembles her offsite already exists: the cohort's orientation, "one block per wave, in the building, with a founder," delivering the why (S7 section 3). It is paid, it is in the building, it forms the group, and it carries the mission and the non-negotiables. It is not called an offsite and is not one; it is named here so that no downstream cluster adds one beside it.

### 7.2 Her parts, each refused or placed

**Her opener** (a personal round on how each person feels, their reflections, and their objectives, modeled by the leader; Book p.309): refused. It is the vulnerability prompt section 6 refuses, and its name is Sŏn's check-in's. Nothing survives under any name.

**Icebreakers** (a personal photo, a favorite book, a walk through one's home on video; Book p.310): refused. Canon's "present without performing" (Canon 1.0, section 01), Ma's "service staff who manufacture activity" (Canon 1.0, section 01), and the house's rule that it does not ask about a person's home (S9 P44) each refuse it alone.

**Agenda structure** (purpose, agenda, limit, notes and actions; Book p.310): placed, already. Every review on the mechanism map has a fixed agenda, a hard stop, and notes with owners that are units (S4 P26, P32, P53). Her PAL is the form the reviews already take, and it needs no offsite to carry it.

**A notetaker per session** (Book p.311): refused as a role; the chair records (S4 P22), the partners' page is the record (S4 P53), the OS surface holds the brief's block (S4 P10).

**Her closer** (a one-to-three-word round, or "what was our most important decision"; Book p.311): refused as a spoken round; its function survives in writing as the house review's reflection paragraph, "one written paragraph appended to the record within the week, read aloud at the next review's opening" (S4 P32), which is her closer with the barometer replaced by a record.

**The shared planning document** and its three benefits, inclusivity, anchoring, and pre-work (Book pp. 308 to 309): absorbed, as the domain read in writing (each partner "writes their questions on it, asynchronously," S4 P53) and the house memo shared twenty-four hours ahead with a reading block (S4 P32). Her point that a shared document gives people "a safe place... without the pressure to debate in the room" is the record's own reason for writing questions on a page rather than standing above someone.

**The offsite as "a collective memory that imprints group understanding"** (Book p.311): absorbed, as the training services and the first quarter, which the house will refer to the way her teams refer to the warehouse with bad heating, and which cost nothing extra.

### 7.3 The workbook's offsite pages, worked

The planning checklist (Workbook p.93) is consumed by the calendar: the reset and the revision have a date on the mechanism map (S4 P39), a room that is not the floor, and pre-reads on the partners' page; its "assign each section to a DRI" is refused (S9 P38, P39); its "send a feedback form to all participants and ask them to rate the offsite" is refused as the survey (S9 I10); its "track all action items until complete" is the partners' page's standing list of open asks (S4 P53). The day-of structure (welcome, check-in exercise, icebreaker, session, check-out exercise; Workbook p.94) is refused in every part but the session. The welcome email is refused; the reset's agenda is on the partners' page. The sample agenda (Workbook p.95) is read for one thing: its longest items are goals and strategic pillars, which at Sŏn are the house review and the gate review, and its social item is a cooking lesson, which at Sŏn is the kitchen's and chef-gated if it exists at all.

### 7.4 The entry test and the freeze

The partners' annual block passes the entry test: its bandwidth cost is the partners' own time at a closed hour; it buys the reset and the revision, which already exist; its runners are the partners with the leads; its record is the reset's versioned decisions. It adds nothing to the map. It cannot fall inside dinner's first quarter, because the first reset is after the quarter by construction (S4 P39), and no other offsite exists to fall there.

**P17 (Recommended).** Sŏn holds no offsite for the house and none for the leads. The partners' mechanism reset and principles revision are held as one closed-hour block per year, away from the building if the partners choose, at no cost to service and with no diagnostic role; that block is her offsite reduced to its decision content. The cohort's orientation block per wave is the one existing gathering that does her forming work and is not an offsite.

**P18 (Recommended).** Her offsite's parts are refused (her opener, icebreakers, a notetaker role, her closer as a spoken round, the feedback form, DRIs per section) or placed where they already run (PAL as every review's fixed agenda; the shared document as the domain read and the house memo; her closer's function as the reflection paragraph). The workbook's planning checklist is consumed by the mechanism map's calendar.

## 8\. Meetings at Sŏn: her meeting material against the mechanism map

### 8.1 What a meeting is here

Her chapter's premise is that "when you think of teams, you think of meetings" (Book p.311). The house has no meeting in her sense during service: the brief opens a service and the close ends it, and both are spoken to a roster that is about to work or has just finished (S4 P10, P12). Everything else that gathers people sits at closed hours (S4 P9). What the map holds that is meeting-shaped: the brief, the close, the check-in, the leads' review, the partners' review, the domain read, the lead-and-partner conversation, the house review, the gate review, the reset, the principles revision, and the whole-house gathering if approved (S4 10.2). Her material is read against each, and what applies is mostly already carried.

### 8.2 Her groundwork and common understanding

"They're only as successful as the relationships between the people involved... invest in creating a common understanding and setting meeting norms up front" (Book pp. 312 to 313): "who's on the team, what each person's role is, and how they prefer to work" (Book p.313). At Sŏn the common understanding is written and read before anyone sits down: the web rendered (S5 `86akh7ru5`), the inventory's rows, the seat sheets, the register, the lead's working-with-me for how the lead prefers to work (S7 P49), and the person page for the person's own account. Her "agree on team norms" is refused as an act a group performs: the norms are the non-negotiables, the register, and the spines, written once, versioned, and the same for every gathering. A team that agreed its own norms would have written a rule with no version and no owner above it, which is drift. Her "extended kickoff meeting to proxy some of the functions of an offsite" (Book p.313) is, for the leads, their first partners' review and first leads' review (S7 14.1), and for the house, the cohort's orientation block.

### 8.3 Her roles

**The DRI**, "the person responsible for the meeting's success" (Book p.313): refused, as Session 9 refused the DRI generally (S9 P38, P39, I15). A meeting-shaped mechanism at Sŏn has an owner on the map (the owner of the room for the brief and the close; the alternating chair for the leads' review; the partners for their review; the center for the house review), and that owner has a range, which is more than a DRI carries.

**The facilitator**, who keeps time, gets through the agenda, tracks participation, and "feels empowered to move the meeting along" (Book pp. 314, 321): absorbed into the chair, whose "only added duty is the clock and the record" (S4 P22). Her rotating facilitator is the alternating chair, and the reason is stronger than hers: "a permanent chair is the first step back toward a general manager" (S4 5.1). The facilitator's participation-tracking ("we've heard a lot from Jen," Book p.318) is refused as a role: the leads' review has three seats and the brief is spoken to a roster that does not debate; the participation rule the house does carry is the domain read's written questions, where every partner writes and no one speaks over another (S4 P53).

**The notetaker**: refused as a role; the record is the mechanism's own. The brief's block is on the OS surface (S4 P10); the close is written by the people who held the tables (S4 P12); the leads' review's notes are the chair's on the team home (S4 5.2); the partners' page is the decision log (S4 P53); the house memo is the record (S4 P32). Her rule that "the best notes... include the top-level discussion topics, decisions made, and follow-ups or action items... with each follow-up assigned an owner and an agreed-upon time frame" (Book p.314) is already every review's form, with the one rule hers lacks: an owner "is a lead, a domain, or a unit, never a person below another" (S4 5.2). Her notes as "psychological safety... if there's a disagreement down the road, you can refer to the meeting notes" is the versioned decision's own purpose (Deck 3.0, p.94). Her notes "shared more widely if you have a transparent culture" is the transparency line, held (`86akh5uby`).

### 8.4 Mutual ownership, purpose, and structure

Her signs of ownership (norms maintained by participants, participation broad, roles rotating; Book p.315) hold at the leads' review by construction: two co-leads, alternating, no one above them. Her "model ownership. Be on time, try not to reschedule" (Book p.315) is the stack's: the leads' review has a day, the check-in is placed by the stack and its moves are counted (S4 P20), and a review that runs into the brief shortens its agenda (S4 5.1). Her "one or two purposes" and PAL (Book pp. 315 to 316) are every review's fixed agenda; the leads' review has eight items in a fixed order and the house review a fixed procedure (S4 P26, P32). Her "Limit" is the hard stop, and the Sŏn rule is sharper: the stop is before the brief and holds every week.

### 8.5 Her norms, each

**Logistics** (Book pp. 316 to 317). Meeting time: fixed on the map, and the leads' review's day moves once, when the early morning opens, to the lowest-tempo day (S4 P22, P25). Delegation: the chef's delegate at the leads' review is chef-gated (S4 P24); a partner cannot delegate a Class A vote (S3 4.5); the room's owner at the brief is the room designation when the Maitre d is absent (S8 P25), which is delegation by rule and never per meeting. Pre-reads: the memo twenty-four hours ahead with a reading block (S4 P32); the leads' review reads the record on the team home; the brief has none, its block is on the surface for anyone who arrives late (S4 P10). Action items: updated on the record before the review, and read first at the house review (S4 P32). Electronics: "no service radio in the room; no stack surface open except the agenda's reads" (S4 P27), and on the floor the phone is pocket-carried with "no visible screen in the dining room" (Canon 1.0, section 08).

**No topics are undiscussable**: section 6.4.

**Be inclusive** (Book p.318): the leads' review's alternation and the domain read in writing; her rule against restating another's idea without credit has no mechanism and needs none in a three-seat room.

**Disagree and commit** (Book p.318): section 11.2.

**Have a parking lot** (Book p.318): refused as a device. An item off the spine at the brief goes to the check-in or the channel; an item off the agenda at the leads' review goes to next week's agenda or the channel, with an owner; there is no lot, because "otherwise, the parking lot will become the town dump" (Book p.318) is exactly what the loop-closure window exists to prevent.

**Respect action items** (Book pp. 318 to 319): every review's notes carry owners and dates, and the leads' review opens on item 2, the captures waiting on a lead past seven days (S4 P26).

**Reconfigure the meeting every three to six months** (Book p.319): the mechanism reset, after the first quarter, after the first year, and annually, reading every mechanism's record, cost, and buy and continuing, changing, or ending it (S4 P39), plus the house review's quarterly reflection paragraph on the review itself (S4 P32). Her three options, refresh the norms, evolve the people and topics, start over, are the reset's three outcomes. Her "consider polling participants or having a neutral person do so" is refused as the survey; the reset reads records.

### 8.6 Her cost argument, and the ledger

"It's a good exercise to calculate how much time you and key members of your company and team spend in meetings. They are costly!" (Book p.312). The bandwidth ledger is that calculation, done in time rather than figures, per team member per month, per lead per week, per partner per week (S4 10.3), and its total for an hourly person is the brief, the close, fifteen minutes of check-in, one pulse question, a recognition when they choose, the review every three to six months, and one paid shift per quarter if the gathering is approved. This page adds nothing to it: the brief's team slot is inside the brief's existing time, the partners' annual block replaces nothing, and no offsite exists. The ledger's own warning stands: the one cost that can exceed its budget is the Maitre d's pre-service windows (S4 P63), and section 9 places the slot's holder with that in view.

### 8.7 The table

| Mechanism | Owner (her DRI) | Chair and record (her facilitator and notetaker) | Norms carried | Refused here |
| ---| ---| ---| ---| --- |
| Shift brief | Owner of the room; room designation when absent | Spoken; readiness block on the OS surface | Fixed spine; languages; hard edge at the scene trigger | Any item about a person; an opener; a script; a parking lot |
| Shift close | Owner of the room; stations by the inward strand | Written by the table holders | Fixed spine; capture shorter than the note | Feedback about a person; a post-mortem |
| Check-in | Lead of the domain | The person page, read back | Three questions, the upward question, one line | A verdict, a task, pay, discipline; a mentor in the room |
| Leads' review | Two co-leads | Alternating chair; notes on the team home | Eight items in order; hard stop; presence rule | A permanent chair; a founder by default; lagging figures |
| Partners' review | The partners | The partners' page, versioned | Fixed agenda ending in the one thing | A delegated Class A vote; a meeting in service hours |
| Domain read | Each partner on the other's page | Written questions | Asynchronous, monthly | Spoken review of a partner |
| House review | The center chairs; leads write | House memo; reflection paragraph | Reading block; prior actions first | Links; P&L; a section on a person |
| Gate review | All partners | Readiness test record | Rows and the variety pass | A gate opened around a failed row |
| Reset and revision | The center with the leads | Versioned decisions | Every mechanism's record, cost, buy | A poll; a person read |
| Whole-house gathering (if approved) | The center | Team home | S4 P38's content; section 9's half | Anything about a person; an announcement |

**P19 (Recommended).** Her meeting material lands on the mechanism map as tabled: the DRI is refused and each mechanism's owner has a range; the facilitator is the alternating chair; the notetaker is the mechanism's own record; norms are the non-negotiables, the register, and the spines, never agreed per group; the parking lot is refused for the loop-closure window; reconfiguration is the reset and the reflection paragraph; her cost argument is the bandwidth ledger, to which this page adds nothing.

## 9\. The brief's team-content slot, and the gathering's team-making half

### 9.1 The slot

Session 4 fixed the brief's spine and bounded a fifth slot, "team content, owned elsewhere, bounded by what time remains before the scene trigger," and its specification refuses "any item about a person; any content that displaces the readiness block; any trigger for a transition in the room" (S4 P10, 13.1). The Realist's rule from that page: the operational block is "a checklist the rush cannot delete," and the team content sits after it, never inside it (S4 3.1). Carryover `86akh67xe` asks this page to design the slot's content inside those bounds.

**What goes in it.** One item per brief, spoken by the owner of the room, chosen from a fixed list in this priority:

1. **The designations' line.** Each designation's holder for the service (the room, the door, the sequence, the pass) says one sentence on what they need from the roster tonight. This is her "meeting roles" reduced to the roster's, and it is the only place a roster hears its own shape in its holders' voices. On a compressed window it is the whole slot, and it is the one item that also serves readiness, which is why it is first.
2. **What the system learned.** One capture from the last close, read as process and never as person: what allowed it, what was updated, what the next server inherits. This is blame the process made audible, and it is the mechanism by which safety to err becomes a thing the roster has heard and not only a rule it read. The reviewing lead chooses it; the room's owner speaks it.
3. **A principle against a moment.** Once a week at most, one sentence from the charter's principles read against something the house did in the last week, spoken by the room's owner. This is the principles revision's raw material (S2 P6.5) reaching the floor in the only form the floor can hear it, and it waits on principles version one (`86akh3tg0`).
4. **A thread added.** A readiness form passed or a fluency connection recorded since the last brief, named as a fact, because the record says a person's growth "adds threads to the collective web" (WP p.11) and the roster is the web on the night. Named like a recognition: read, not editorialized. It is fourth because it names a person, and the rule below governs how.

**What may never be in it.** Anything about a person beyond a fact the person page already shows (a form passed, a first solo held), and never a read, a rating, a comparison, or a correction. A script for the service. A survey question or a poll. An opener about how anyone feels. A personal share or an icebreaker. A sales or upsell instruction. A lagging figure. A structure change announced, because a change reaches the team by four channels and never by announcement (S8 P49). A build item, because the seam forbids it (S4 P9). Anything that runs past the scene trigger.

**Length.** The slot has no floor and its ceiling is bounded by the scene trigger. The team sets its ceiling, as a reset parameter, at five minutes on a full pre-service window and zero on a compressed one, where a compressed window is one on which the readiness block ran in its thirty-second form. Five minutes is a duration and not a financial figure; it is flagged for the reset, which reads the first quarter's brief records for how often the slot ran at all.

**Who holds it.** The owner of the room for that period runs the brief (S4 P11, ruled to the Maitre d), and on services the Maitre d does not work the room designation runs it (S8 P25), holding the slot with the same list and the same refusals. The room designation's card (S8 `86akhcz4g`) gains the slot's list. The kitchen's item, if the pass owner speaks at item 1, is chef-gated.

**By period.** Dinner as stated. The early morning's brief is a window brief whose slot is item 1 alone, because its designation set is smaller and its window shorter (S8 P8). Late night carries no second brief and no second slot: where periods run back to back with the same crew, the second brief is "a thirty-second readiness insert, never a second gathering" (S4 P14). Lunch has no charter and no brief.

**How it is read.** The slot produces no line about anyone. Its only record is the brief's record on the OS surface noting which item ran or that the slot was dropped, so that the reset can count briefs with a slot against briefs without across the quarter. A slot dropped on most briefs of a quarter is read as sequence corruption on the brief's window, a window problem and not a lead's, and it is one of the two environment-side sources section 15 adds to cooling failure's line.

### 9.2 The whole-house gathering's team-making half, if approved

Session 4 wrote the gathering as conditional and founder-gated: on the same closed day as the house review, after it, paid as a scheduled shift, carrying the review's one thing, the quarter's goal-page states, the recognitions of the quarter, and the next quarter's goals, and nothing about a person (S4 P38). The bandwidth ledger already prices it: one paid shift per quarter per person (S4 10.3). This page designs the half Session 4 left, inside those bounds.

**The team-making half, in order after Session 4's content.**

1. **The threads of the quarter.** The forms passed and the fluency connections recorded in the quarter, read as facts like recognitions. This is the web growing, said aloud once a quarter to the whole web.
2. **What the house learned.** The captures of the quarter that changed a process, as process. The floor wrote them; the house hears what it wrote.
3. **The principles read back.** The moments of the quarter against the principles, spoken by the center, which is the principles revision's read-back reaching the room that produced the moments (S2 P6.5). At the first two gatherings this is the revision itself, as Session 3 tied it (S3 P11.7).
4. **Coverage.** The seats opened in the quarter and the pool read, as coverage only and nothing about anyone who left (S9 P30).
5. **One open question.** One question the reset or the house review could not close, put to the house with the feedback channel as its destination and a stated window. This is the item that makes "a say in the rules" a mechanism (section 3.9): the floor is asked, once a quarter, in the one room it is in, and its answer has a place to go.

**Refused in it.** A personal opener or closer, an icebreaker, the work style exercise, a survey, a speech about culture, and any structure change announced there rather than already reached by the four channels. Nothing about a person beyond a fact on their page.

**If declined.** The review's outcome reaches the house by the three channels only (S4 P38). What the house loses: the one occasion the whole house is in one room, so that the record's "every element in relationship with every other" (WP p.8) has fewer relationships across periods and services than the structure can otherwise produce; the principles' read-back stays written; and the floor's say in the rules stays indirect, read from its records and never asked. The team's recommendation stands with Sessions 3 and 4: approve, at a cost in closed service the founders weigh, with the content bounded as above.

**P20 (Recommended).** The brief's team slot carries one item from a fixed list in priority: the designations' one line each, what the system learned from the last close as process, a principle against a moment once a week at most, and a thread added as a fact. It refuses anything about a person beyond a page fact, a script, a survey, an opener, a personal share, a lagging figure, an announced change, and a build item. It ends at the scene trigger, has a ceiling of five minutes on a full window and zero on a compressed one as a reset parameter, is held by the owner of the room or the room designation, is item 1 alone at the early morning's window brief, and produces no record but which item ran.

**P21 (Recommended).** If the whole-house gathering is approved, its team-making half carries, after Session 4's content, the quarter's threads, what the house learned, the principles read back, coverage, and one open question put to the house with the channel as its destination. It refuses an opener, an icebreaker, the grid, a survey, a culture speech, and any announcement. If declined, the floor's say in the rules stays indirect and the page says so.

**P22 (Founder-gated).** Whether the whole-house gathering exists (`86akh5uc7`, `86akh673u`, extending S3 P11.7 and S4 P38, not filed twice). The team recommends approval with the half above.

**P23 (Chef-gated).** The pass owner's line at item 1 of the slot, and the kitchen's brief.

**P24 (Team-filled).** The slot's ceiling revisited at the first reset from the first quarter's brief records, and the count of briefs on which it ran.

## 10\. Operator mode and creator mode

Her distinction: operator meetings have agendas and are for "decisions, updates, priorities, and alignment"; creator meetings are for brainstorming, "much less structure," and may produce nothing but ideas; a good team has both, and the creator time is built "primarily through offsites" (Book pp. 319 to 320). Her example is an operator question about a balance sheet that became an unconstrained five-year vision.

**Where creation happens at Sŏn, and when.** On the build metronome, which is "fast by system, never by grind" (S1 section 2), and in the pre-opening cadence, which is one long creator period at the partners' weekly working meeting (S4 9.2). In service: the mechanism reset and the principles revision, annually, at a closed hour (section 7); the charter drafting group for a new period, convened when a period is drafted and dissolved when it is ruled (S8 P41); the menu turn, the chef's (S4 P36); the content engine, Brandon's, daily (WP p.31); and module authorship by any qualified team member, paid (WP p.19; S7 P33). The floor's creator mode is the last two of those and the feedback channel's "suggest improvements" (WP p.22); the floor is never convened to brainstorm, because a convened floor is a meeting in service hours or a closed service.

**What never happens in the room during service.** Any creation. The seam protection forbids a build meeting in the building during service hours (S4 P9), and her balance-sheet moment, an operator item that turns into a strategy brainstorm, is exactly what the protection exists to stop from happening in a dining room in dinner's first quarter, when "the build engine is idling and the founders are in the room" (S1 section 2). Inside the leads' review it is refused by the hard stop: an item that opens into a creator conversation goes to the partners' page as an ask with an owner. At the partners' review pre-opening it is the meeting's own purpose, and in service it belongs to the reset. The service metronome is set by the register and the table (S1); creation runs on the other clock.

**Her personal typology** ("some people are operators, and some people are makers or creators," Book p.319): refused as a type. The strands are two kinds of work and not two kinds of person (S5 P7), and the house reads no one for temperament (section 13).

**P25 (Recommended).** Creation at Sŏn runs on the build metronome and at closed hours: the pre-opening partners' review, the annual reset and revision, a charter drafting group dissolved at its ruling, the menu turn, the content engine, and paid module authorship. Nothing creative happens in the room during service, the leads' review's hard stop routes a creator item to the partners' page, and the operator-or-creator typology of persons is refused.

## 11\. Decision-making in meetings

### 11.1 Her five methods, against the register

Her methods: autocratic, consensus, democratic, consultative, delegated (Book p.324), and her rule is to be explicit about which one is running and who decides (Book p.321). At Sŏn the method is fixed by the register before any room exists, which is her rule made structural: "the range within which that owner acts without asking is stated in advance" (S3 4.1). The owner decides inside a range, which is her autocratic method bounded by a range and a trigger. Class B is consultative by rule: "the owning domain decides; any domain whose outcomes are affected is consulted before the event, not informed after" (S3 4.3). Class A is neither consensus nor democratic: with two partners it is "both or neither, with the status quo as default" (S3 4.5, held under `86akh5u77`), and with three the record's one instance is lunch as "an equal decision among all three partners" (WP p.36; S4 P57, founder-gated). Delegated is the register's own form, "ranges set one level out" (S3 4.1, rule 3), and never a per-decision act. Nothing at Sŏn is decided by a vote in a room, and nothing is decided by a room. Her closing example, "I'm the decision-maker. I'd like to consult all of you, but I will ultimately decide" (Book pp. 324 to 325), is the register's entry read aloud, and it is read before the meeting rather than at it.

The interim two-partner rule is the founders' own meeting decision process and it is not this page's to land; the partners' review "runs on whatever rule is ratified and holds the status quo until one is" (S4 P54).

### 11.2 Disagree and commit, and the senior person speaking last

**Disagree and commit** (Book p.318): absorbed, with the disagreement written. A decision inside another owner's range is theirs; an objection has a destination, the Class B or C hold as a joint half-page (S8 P50); once the owner decides, the objection is on the record and the decision stands. What replaces "commit to supporting its success" as a norm is the read-back: every change is read back on the next scorecard by the source that raised it (S9 P26), so a decision that was not supported shows as a mechanism not cleared, on a record, and not as a person's attitude. Her leader saying "I'm going to disagree and commit" (Book p.327) survives as a founder writing a question on a domain page and leaving the domain owner's decision standing (S4 P53).

**The most senior person holds their opinion until the end** (Book p.326; the editor's pull quote at Book pp. 329 to 330): survives whole where it has an object. The record's rooms are parallel, so in the leads' review there is no senior person. Where a founder attends the leads' review by standing invitation (S4 P22), the founder speaks last, and the rule is written into section 17.6's entry. The monthly domain read is speaking last by construction: each partner writes questions on the other's page after reading it whole, and the domain owner answers (S4 P53). The lead-and-partner conversation is on the lead's page with the partner writing questions (S4 P59). Her exception, a leader putting forward a provocative idea to elicit a reaction, belongs to the partners' review pre-opening and to no room in service.

### 11.3 Frameworks, logs, and the personality callout

**Decision-making frameworks** (RAPID, SPADE, a seven-step process; Book p.326): refused as frameworks. The register's form, owner, range, triggers with destinations, is the one framework the house teaches, and it is what the why block delivers as vocabulary (S9 13.4). A second framework beside it would be two rules for one decision.

**Decision logs** (Book pp. 326 to 327): survive as the records the mechanisms already write, and never as "a spreadsheet of every decision your team has made." The partners' page is "a decision log by versioned decision" (S4 P53; Deck 3.0, p.94); the goal page carries its change record with the reason and what it displaced (S4 P35); the inventory has a version log (S8 P49); the mechanism map has a log (S9 I4). Her reason for mixed success, that logs "are most effective when they're widely adopted and rigorously kept current" (Book p.327), is why Sŏn's logs are the mechanisms' own records and not a separate artifact anyone has to remember to keep. Her "edit the log when a decision has been changed and explain why" is the versioned change with its reason field (S9 P24, P25).

**"Decision-making and personality types"** (Book p.325): refused. Her exercise places each person on a square of the decision process and reads where they are stuck. At Sŏn no decision is the group's, so there is no process for a group to stand on, and the grid is never used to read another person (section 13). What her exercise wanted, a way to say "we are blocked and here is why," is the hold's half-page: the problem, the options, the trade-offs, written jointly (S8 P50).

**P26 (Recommended).** Her five decision methods are replaced by the register: the owner decides inside a range; Class B is consultative by rule; Class A is both or neither with the status quo as default, held under `86akh5u77`; delegation is ranges set one level out. Disagree and commit survives with the disagreement written as a hold and the commitment replaced by the read-back. The senior person speaks last survives for a founder in any room and is the domain read's own form.

**P27 (Recommended).** Decision frameworks are refused for the register's one form; decision logs survive as the partners' page, the goal page's change record, the inventory's log, and the mechanism map's log, never as a separate spreadsheet; the personality-types exercise is refused and its function is the hold's joint half-page.

**P28 (Founder-gated).** The interim two-partner rule as the founders' meeting decision process (`86akh5u77`, extended and not filed twice), and the three-partner rule beyond the one instance the record states (S4 P57).

## 12\. Leadership team meetings

### 12.1 The first team

Her "first team," from Lencioni, is the rule that "leaders must make a commitment to the success of their first team, the leadership team, above that of their second team, the one they directly lead" (Book p.329). Refused as a priority ordering and absorbed as a structure. The two leads "are parallel. Neither reports to the other. They are co-leads of different systems serving the same center" (WP p.10), and the leads' review is their standing integration (S4 P59). But the web has no altitude: a lead whose loyalty ran to the leads' review above their domain would be standing above the domain in the way the ledger's departure from her hierarchy refuses, and the record's whole argument is that the edge is the most sensitive position, not the least (WP p.9). What her point protects, a leader who withholds their domain's reality from the leadership room, is at Sŏn sequence corruption at the interface: a Class B hold never written, a domain line never carried into the leads' review, an interface read that shows handoffs breaking with nothing on the record (S9 3.3). The commitment is to the record, not to a team above one's own.

### 12.2 Stripe's cadence, as far as p.330 carries it

**Monday morning, three hours**: snippets in a document by Sunday evening, then metrics, the product calendar, leadership hiring, and topics from the snippets (Book p.329). At Sŏn the leads' review's eight items do the metrics and priorities in a fixed order with a hard stop before the brief, not three hours (S4 P26); leadership hiring is the pipeline read's line under item 6 (S5 P28); the product calendar is the menu turn's calendar, chef-gated (S4 P36), and the charter placement calendar (S4 section 8); the snippets are answered by Session 3, "The shift close is the edge's snippet, daily. The lead's weekly note is the center's, and the leads' review agenda is derived from both" (S3 P10.3), and the workbook's snippets template (Workbook pp. 96 to 97) is consumed by the close's spine and the lead's note, with its "info on top talent" refused as a line about a person and its "customer issues" and "customer wins" carried by the captures and the recognitions. Internal communication depth is S11's. The partners' review is the founders' weekly and it reads the leads' record rather than re-running it (S4 P28).

**Thursday afternoon, one hour**: only the heading falls in range; its paragraph is Session 11's. What this page can say from the heading alone is that the leads have no second weekly meeting and the partners' review has no creator hour; the monthly lead-and-partner conversation, in the check-in's form on the lead's own page (S4 P59), is the nearest thing and it is not a social hour. The rest waits for Session 11.

### 12.3 Expanding the senior leadership team

Her callout: the senior team is small and changes infrequently, prospective leaders are told a seat on it is not guaranteed, and Stripe built a supplemental leadership team, then retired it for an operating group with a monthly meeting (Book p.330). At Sŏn the leadership lines are fixed by the record's leadership delta, "roughly eight leadership lines running the full span of the day against fourteen running one dinner service" (WP p.22), and a line is added only when a period's variety pass at its gate requires one, "argued and ratified before the period opens" (S8 P8). No supplemental team, no LT beside an ST, no operating group. A Station Lead or the Head of Beverage does not join a leadership meeting by seniority; the kitchen's seat at the leads' review is chef-gated (S4 P24) and the Head of Beverage's line sits under the Maitre d's read (S8 P9; `86akhcz1u`). Her transparency with prospective leaders is the transparency sheet, which states the web and the direct lead (S5 7.3) and has no executive team to promise; a lead hired later enters at the lead seat's entry horizon and at no rank (S8 P31). Her closing lesson, "keep a tight group at the helm and not end up with 20 or 30 people in the room debating key company decisions" (Book p.330), is the register: the reserved classes are the partners' and nothing is debated by a room (S3 4.3).

**P29 (Recommended).** The first team is refused as a priority ordering and absorbed as the leads' commitment to the record: a domain's reality withheld from the leads' review is sequence corruption at the interface. Stripe's Monday is the leads' review's eight items with a hard stop, the pipeline read's line, the menu and charter calendars, and the close and the lead's note as snippets (S3 P10.3). No supplemental leadership team exists; a line is added only by a period's variety pass at its gate.

## 13\. The work style grid's team use

### 13.1 What is settled and what is open

The grid is out of recruiting (S5 P8), lives inside the working-with-me document as a self-awareness exercise for founders and leads (S1 8.2; S7 P53), and never enters structure, scheduling, or placement (S8 P40). Three carryovers (`86akh7qq7`, `86akhb2wj`, `86akhcz6v`) route one question here: whether it has any team use, "as language people use about themselves and never as an instrument that reads a person for a seat."

### 13.2 The decision

The grid has no team use beyond the placement Sessions 1 and 7 already hold, and this page adds one narrow use in one direction. The reasons:

1. A language a team uses "about itself," on a roster that dissolves every service, is a language people use about each other. Her own illustration is a leader in a meeting saying a colleague is "acting a bit 'red'" (Book p.328), which is a read of a person spoken in a room, and the house refuses a read of a person anywhere but the person's own line (S9 P42).
2. The record's vocabulary for difference is the strands, "two kinds of work, not two kinds of person" (S5 3.3), and canon's for the floor is Nunchi and Jeong. A second vocabulary about persons would compete with the one about work, and on a floor the vocabulary about persons wins, because it is easier to say.
3. Four names are a typology, and a typology on a floor becomes a placement within a week: "the room needs a Director tonight" is the sentence S8 P40 exists to forbid, and it would be said at the brief where designations are named.
4. An hourly person is never asked to write a working-with-me (S7 P49), so there is no surface on which a floor person could place themselves that is not a form the house holds about them; and the person page refuses a rating (S4 P18), which a self-placement read by a lead is.
5. The one use her material has for it that the house needs, "a common language" for founders and leads who "work in separate domains" (S1 8.2), is already met where it lives.

**The one narrow use.** A lead's working-with-me is readable by the lead's domain on the team home (S7 P49). The lead's self-placement is therefore language the domain may use about the lead, upward, at the check-in's fourth question and on the channel, because the lead wrote it about themselves for that reason. The reverse never happens. A person who wants the vocabulary for themselves can read Session 1's instrument on the team home and place themselves in their own head; nothing records it.

**How misuse is caught.** The grid's four names appearing on any person page, scorecard, schedule note, designation block, brief record, close, sheet, or leads' review line fails readiness row 120 (section 18), which is a search like S9's row 115. A check-in line in a person's own words saying a lead placed them on it is a range breach on the lead's check-in entry (section 17.5) and goes to whoever holds a lead's check-in (`86akhb2jg`); until that closes, it goes to the partners' review as a load reading on the lead.

**P30 (Recommended).** The work style grid has no team use beyond its placement inside a lead's working-with-me document. Its one team-facing use is upward and one-directional: a lead's domain may use the lead's own self-placement about the lead. It never appears on any record about a person, never names a designation's need, and never enters a room as a read of anyone; its four names on any such record fail a readiness row.

## 14\. Community after the cohort, the mentor after the plan, and designations as rotation

### 14.1 Community in the steady state

Her onboarding wanted "a sense of community with other new hires," and Session 7 found it met pre-opening by the cohort itself, "the community her section wants is the cohort itself and needs no mechanism" (S7 section 3). A later hire arrives alone into a running house. Whether the steady state needs a mechanism is carryover `86akhb2wj`'s question.

The team's position: no new mechanism, and an honest partial. What does the work for a person arriving alone: the mentor from the pool, same strand and domain, matched for language and overlap (S7 P41); the paired services as "the teaching body" (S7 P42); the brief's one thing naming the seat's new holder as a fact (S6 P71) and, on this page, the slot's fourth item naming their first solo as a thread added; the peer recognition platform, where the roster's voice reaches them; and the house's own precedent that community is transmitted by mentoring and not manufactured, since the first wave mentors the second (S7 P8). A batched start date, so that later hires arrive as a small cohort, is a hiring-calendar choice the hiring partner and the leads can make when the pipeline allows (S6 3.9) and it is noted as an option, not recommended as a culture mechanism, because a calendar that waits for a cohort holds a seat open longer than the pool read allows.

What remains partial is the thing section 3.6 named: the record built belonging in full for the customer and for the team wrote a break space. Belonging among the team is not a condition the philosophy names and is the outcome the conditions produce (section 2.3), and the read of it is the pulse and, over time, retention read as tension-loss departures by count (S9 P13). The one direct mechanism the house has is the whole-house gathering, founder-gated. This page does not invent another, because every candidate (a social, a meal, an outing) is either the staff meal the record is silent on (P12) or a manufactured activity Ma refuses.

### 14.2 The mentor as a standing relationship

Session 7: the relationship runs "through the plan and after it as the person chooses," said at the fifth check-in, with the stack stopping the overlap at the plan's close (S7 P42). Session 9 recorded the shape the person states in the career conversation block, in the person's words (S9 I7). What the house does with it after the plan, designed here:

Nothing formal, by design. The house records only the shape the person stated and takes no further act, because a recorded standing relationship is a line about two people, and the person page refuses lines about anyone but the person in their own words. What the house may do: where the person states "continue," the stack may treat overlap with the former mentor as a scheduling preference of the person's, like any preference on the sheet, honored where the schedule allows and never required, and written nowhere on the mentor's page. What the house refuses: the mentor becoming a sponsor or an advocate ("The system is the advocate," WP p.11); a coach, which is S12's and founder-gated as a spend for leads (S7 P22); a channel for the lead, which S7 P42 already refuses; or a person the lead asks about the former mentee. The mentor's later place in the house is the pool: the former mentee becomes eligible to mentor once their own plan has closed with its goal held (S7 P41), which is how the relationship reproduces without being recorded. The mentor's own mentoring is recognized beyond shift only if Session 13 says so (S7 P35).

### 14.3 Designations as rotation, never status

Session 8 holds that a designation is named at the brief, lasts one service, and is never permanent (S8 P22, P24, P25); Session 9 holds that a designation held by one person every service for a quarter is a reset question about the seat's hours and the designation's rule, "never a second seat and never a read of the holder" (S9 P32). Carryover `86akhcz6v` asks this page to hold designations rotating as a development mechanism and not a status.

The rule this page adds is the rotation floor, written as part of each designation's rule on the register (section 17.4): among the seats eligible for a designation on a service (a complete readiness form and range card, no non-negotiable line; S8 P25), no eligible person holds it on every service they work in a quarter while another eligible person held it on none. The floor is a rule about the roster's shape and not about anyone's performance; its read is the count per quarter the stack surfaces to the reset (S9 I3's third rule), and the reset's three branches are Session 9's (the schedule or a rotation floor; the eligible pool widened by forms placed on the schedule; a rotation floor against preference). Development is the reason: holding the room once is the way a range is rehearsed at scale, and the eligible pool widening by forms is the path making itself visible.

Never a status, stated as refusals: a designation carries no pay line (S13's), no mark on the person page beyond the brief's record, no title, and no place on a sheet; it is never named as a reward or withheld as a sanction, and feedback to a holder is Session 12's (`86akhcz71`); its count is never read as the holder's performance (S9 P32; `86akhcz7b`). A lead who names the same person every night "because they are good at it" has, by the third quarter, made a permanent room holder under another name, which is a refused carrier (S9 P36).

**P31 (Recommended).** The steady state needs no new community mechanism: the mentor from the pool, the paired services, the brief naming the new holder and the first solo, and the recognition platform do the work for a person arriving alone, and belonging among the team is read as an outcome by the pulse and tension-loss departures. The partial is named: the record builds belonging for the customer in full and for the team as a break space, and the one direct team mechanism is the gathering, founder-gated.

**P32 (Recommended).** After the plan the house records only the shape the person stated and takes no further act; a stated "continue" is a scheduling preference of the person's, honored where the schedule allows and written on no one's page. The mentor never becomes a sponsor, a coach, or a channel for the lead; the relationship reproduces through the pool.

**P33 (Recommended).** Each designation's rule carries a rotation floor: no eligible person holds it on every service they work in a quarter while another eligible person held it on none, read by the stack's count at the reset and never as the holder's performance. A designation carries no pay line, no page mark, no title, and is never a reward or a sanction.

## 15\. Bandwidth as the environment's primary read

Carryover `86akh5uw3` says "Session 10 uses bandwidth as the team environment's primary read," written before Session 9 placed every team-state read in the diagnostic. The two reconcile without conflict: bandwidth is the environment's primary read, and it is expressed through cooling failure's evidence line (S9 P13) and the bandwidth ledger (S4 10.3), and through no new read. The record's order is the reason: "Bandwidth is the organizational metabolic rate... An organization running on building logic cannot \[engineer for this\], because it has no way to measure bandwidth. It measures output" (WP p.12). A team environment read by anything other than bandwidth first would be reading output.

**What the environment reads, and through which line.** Cooling failure's line already carries the pulse composite, the thermal-load lines, the bandwidth flag on goals, tension-loss departures by count, check-in friction lines aggregated, feedback items past thirty days, seam breaches, and exit interviews read for the building (S9 P13). This page adds two environment-side sources to that line and nothing else: the count of briefs on which the team slot was dropped (section 9.1), read as a window taken; and the count of closes on which the note displaced the capture or the capture the note, which Session 4 named as a finding on the close window's length (S4 finding 14.3) and which reads as the close window taken. Both are counts of services and both are on records the OS surface already holds.

**A goal met at a bandwidth cost.** The goal page's fourth state (S4 P35): scored "as a system failure at the time, not reflected on afterward," it is cooling failure's evidence line (S9 4.7), the fix is removing the friction named, and its allocation consequence, "covers come down before the floor is thinned, and a service period that consumes the team's bandwidth is restructured before it is defended on its results" (S3's attachment to `86akh3t00`), is founder-gated and the line states the dependency. Session 14 must not build a performance tier that rewards the result (carryover to S14 already on `86akh5uw3`). What this page adds: an environment mechanism that met its purpose at a bandwidth cost fails the same way. A brief whose team slot ran every night on a window that had to compress the readiness block to fit it, or a gathering held on a day that closed a service the house could not afford to close, is a mechanism met at a bandwidth cost, and the reset reads it as cooling failure on the mechanism, not as a success of the environment.

**What the environment cannot yet read.** The cultural labor score is undefined (`86akh5u9x`), so cooling failure's line carries "cannot read yet" for it and the pulse's one question is the only defined read of how the team is doing; the close window's length is unstated, so the second source above is a count against no allocation; and slack in the labor model is a figure this program does not hold. The environment's primary read has one defined line and three stated gaps.

**P34 (Recommended).** Bandwidth is the environment's primary read, expressed through cooling failure's evidence line and the bandwidth ledger and through no new read; `86akh5uw3` and S9 P13 are reconciled as one rule. Two environment-side sources are added to the line: briefs with the slot dropped and closes with the capture or the note displaced, both as counts of services. A culture mechanism met at a bandwidth cost is read as cooling failure on the mechanism.

**P35 (Founder-gated).** The allocation consequence of a cooling-failure fix, "the order is the decision" (`86akh3t00`, extended and not filed twice), on which the read of a goal or a mechanism met at a bandwidth cost depends for its consequence.

## 16\. The founder side, to the ceiling, and the customer side where a team mechanism builds it

### 16.1 The founders

Canon's obligation runs to founders (Canon 1.0, section 01; Deck 3.0, p.14) and specifies nothing for them (section 2.1). The ten conditions, read for the two founders and the chef partner as far as the record carries them:

Legible rules: the founding seat descriptions with interiority excluded (S2; `86akh3x9m` to S16), non-overlapping domains (WP p.3), and Class A's list (S3 4.3). A stated range: the partners' review's agenda and the reserved classes, with the interim two-partner rule held (`86akh5u77`). Judgment: not applicable in the employee sense; the founders' judgment is the domain's. Safety to err: Principle 4, "blame the process, and the founders' processes first" (S1), and the record's own admission, "Sŏn has done it too, which is how the team knows the trap" (WP p.17). Safety to speak: the domain read in writing, "how equal partners review each other's domains without either standing above the other" (S4 P53), and the record's no-surprises rule applied upward (S1, principle 4). Being known: the working-with-me documents, exchanged, and the grid inside them (S1 8.2). A path: not in the record; the founders' own learning tempo is Session 16's (S1, founder-gated; `86akh2qzy`). Time not taken: the founders' floor presence on the service metronome (S1; S4 P9) and the build tempo "fast by system, never by grind" (S1), with no read of the founders' own bandwidth, "the nervous system does not read the center" (`86akh2qzy`, to S16). A say in the rules: they own them. A place of their own: not in the record.

The founder side is therefore stronger than the employee side on rules, range, and say, because the founders wrote the rules, and weaker on time and a path, because the record was written by the founders about the team and reads the center nowhere. Everything about who the founders are, what they value, and how they work is interiority and routes to Session 16; nothing of it is recorded here as a position.

**The chef partner.** Legible rules: canon's held sequence in fixed order, "Session 1B closes before Brand Narrative opens... then Session 7C... last, Session 11A" (Deck 3.0, p.88), and the record's seat as "an equal founding partner, freed from carrying the rest of the business alone" (WP p.3), held against canon's pending hire (`86akh2qrp`). A stated range: culinary execution during service as a designation and culinary direction overall (WP p.10), with every kitchen entry chef-gated. A say in the rules: lunch as a three-partner decision (WP p.36), and the partners' review once the sequence has run (S4 P55). The rest of the chef's conditions are the chef's to shape and are marked so.

### 16.2 The customer side, only where a team mechanism builds it

Three customer conditions are built by team mechanisms this page holds, and are named so that the coupling is visible. The server's range (section 3.2) is the customer's condition: "service authority distributed to the closest-to-customer position" is on canon's Playground list (Canon 1.0, section 01), and a server with no range cannot build agency for a table. The David protocol as "a system decision, never a floor call" (Canon 1.0, section 08) is a rule the team holds so that one customer's condition does not depend on which server is on. And "we walk, we never point" (Canon 1.0, section 06) is a rule the team holds that builds the customer's condition of not being routed. The rest of the customer's playground is canon's and not the team's.

**P36 (Recommended).** The founder side of the philosophy is as tabled: rules, range, and say are mechanisms because the founders own them; safety to err and to speak are Principle 4 and the domain read; being known is the working-with-me exchange; a path and time not taken have no read in the record and route to Session 16. Nothing about the founders' interiority is recorded.

**P37 (Founder-gated).** The founders' own bandwidth read and learning tempo (`86akh2qzy`, extended and not filed twice), the one employee condition the founder side lacks entirely.

**P38 (Chef-gated).** The chef partner's conditions beyond canon's held sequence, the designation, and the lunch vote.

## 17\. Decision rights for the environment

Every entry in the ledger's form: owner; range as may and may not; triggers, each with a named destination. An entry the record cannot furnish is marked incomplete and never filled by analogy.

### 17.1 Holding the brief's team slot

Owner. The owner of the room for that period, the Maitre d under the ruling; on services the Maitre d does not work, the room designation. The kitchen's item at the slot's first line: chef-gated.

Range. May speak one item from the list in section 9.1 in its priority; may drop the slot on a compressed window; may choose which capture is read as process, on the reviewing lead's selection; may let each designation's holder speak their one line. May not speak about a person beyond a fact on their page; may not add a script, a survey, an opener, a personal prompt, a sales instruction, or a lagging figure; may not announce a structure change; may not run past the scene trigger; may not let the slot displace or compress the readiness block.

Triggers. An item about a person spoken at the brief goes to the lead's check-in holder as a range breach on the room's owner (`86akhb2jg`), and until that closes, to the partners' review as a load reading on the lead. A slot dropped on most briefs of a quarter goes to the reset as a window read under cooling failure. An item that would change a range, trigger, or mechanism goes to the standing change line and not to the slot. A kitchen-side item goes to the chef seat.

Complete for the floor; the kitchen's line chef-gated.

### 17.2 Calling or declining an offsite

Owner. The partners, for the annual block; no one else may call one.

Range. May hold the mechanism reset and the principles revision as one block at a closed hour, away from the building if they choose; may invite the leads as the reset already does. May not close a service for it; may not hold any gathering inside dinner's first quarter; may not hold one for the house without the whole-house gathering's ruling; may not read team state from it; may not add an opener, an icebreaker, a closer round, or a feedback form to it.

Triggers. A proposal to close a service for any gathering goes to the whole-house gathering's ruling (`86akh5uc7`, `86akh673u`) and to Class A if it is a new cost class. A proposal for a leads' offsite goes to the reset's agenda as the reset. A gathering proposed inside the freeze goes to the partners' page marked held for the first reset.

Complete.

### 17.3 Changing a meeting-shaped mechanism's norms or form

Owner. The reset, for the room's mechanisms (the brief, the close, the check-in, the leads' review); the partners' review, for the founder cadence's; the leads' review, for a parameter inside a range it already holds; the center, for the house review's procedure.

Range. May continue, change by versioned decision, or end a mechanism at the reset (S4 P39); may set a parameter inside a held range between resets and log it. May not change a spine, an interval, a day, an agenda, or a hard stop inside dinner's first quarter; may not change any norm by agreement in the room; may not change a norm by a lead's announcement; may not add a meeting without the four-part entry test and the six-question playground test.

Triggers. A change proposed inside the freeze goes to the partners' page marked held. A change without a reason line goes back to its proposer through the chair. A new meeting proposed goes to the entry test at the leads' review and to the reset for its playground test. A norm changed by agreement or announcement fails row 122 and goes to the leads' review.

Complete.

### 17.4 Naming a designation's rotation rule

Owner. The reset, on the Maitre d's proposal for the floor's designations, the Head of Beverage's for beverage's, the chef seat's for the kitchen's (S9 16.5).

Range. May set a rotation floor as part of the designation's rule; may widen the eligible pool by forms placed on the schedule; may change the schedule's placement of the seat's services. May not make a designation a status, a pay line, a title, a page mark, or a sheet field; may not name it as a reward or withhold it as a sanction; may not read the holder's performance from the count; may not create a permanent holder or a second seat.

Triggers. A designation held by one person every service for a quarter goes to the reset (S9 P32). A designation that cannot be named on a service because no one is eligible goes to the training-infrastructure line and the leads' review that week (S9 16.5). A designation named as a reward or withheld as a sanction goes to the lead's check-in holder as a range breach.

Complete for the floor and beverage; the kitchen's chef-gated.

### 17.5 Running the grid as language

Owner. A lead, about themselves only, inside their working-with-me; the lead's domain, about the lead, upward.

Range. A lead may place themselves and revise the placement; the domain may use the lead's placement at the check-in's fourth question and on the channel. No one may place another person; no one may name a designation's need in the grid's words; no record about a person may carry the four names; no module teaches it and no mentor is matched by it.

Triggers. The four names on any person page, scorecard, schedule note, designation block, brief record, close, sheet, or leads' review line fail row 120 and go to the leads' review. A person's check-in line stating a lead placed them on it goes to the lead's check-in holder (`86akhb2jg`), and until that closes, to the partners' review as a load reading on the lead.

Complete.

### 17.6 Correcting behavior in a meeting-shaped mechanism

Owner. The chair for the leads' review; the owner of the room for the brief and the close; the center for the house review and the gathering; the partners for their review.

Range. May hold the clock, decline an item off the spine or the agenda, and end at the stop; may refuse a unilateral Class B case until written jointly; may require a founder attending by invitation to speak last. May not speak about a person in the room; may not correct a person in front of the roster or the house; may not name anyone's work style; may not carry a correction into the record.

Triggers. A person-level correction goes to that person's check-in, at the next scheduled one, and its content is Session 12's. A non-negotiable surfaced in any room goes to both leads that day (S7 P45). A founder who spoke first at the leads' review goes to the partners' page as a seam note on the presence rule.

Complete.

### 17.7 Incomplete entries, named

The kitchen's entries throughout: chef-gated on `86akh2qrp`. The holder of a lead's check-in, which every range breach on a lead's entry above needs as a destination: `86akhb2jg`. Whether the house has a closed day, on which the reviews and the gathering would sit: `86akh6739`. Whether the whole-house gathering exists: `86akh5uc7`, `86akh673u`. The employee area and the lockers, which "a place of their own" needs as a zone: `86akhb2kb`. Whether the pre-service window carries a staff meal, and its kitchen cost: P12 and P13. The owner of canon, for the "emotional standard of the room" no versioned document holds beyond canon's service model (section 4.1): `86akh3t3y`. The interim two-partner rule under every partners' review entry: `86akh5u77`. The cultural labor score's line: `86akh5u9x`.

**P39 (Recommended).** The decision-rights entries 17.1 to 17.6 as written, complete where marked complete.

**P40 (Founder-gated).** The incomplete entries in 17.7, none filled by analogy: the kitchen's, the lead's check-in holder, the closed day, the gathering, the employee area, the staff meal, canon's owner, the partner rule, and the score's line.

## 18\. Readiness rows

Sessions 3 to 9 wrote rows 1 to 118, and the test is one instrument: a row is met by a condition holding, never by a document existing; a row that depends on a founder-gated or chef-gated item says so inside the row and is read as failed at the gate review until it closes, never waived. Rows already carrying environment conditions are not repeated: rows 8, 9, and 10 (the brief and the close running), row 95 (the room held on every service), row 102 (a structure change by versioned entry and no announcement), row 109 (the recurrence rules including the designation count), row 113 (a departure's coverage line and nothing about the person), and row 115 (no DRI, survey, or delegation framework on the team home). The rows below are what the environment must have running before dinner's gate, and, where stated, at the first reset.

| 119\. The work style grid's four names appear on no person page, scorecard, schedule note, designation block, brief record, close, seat sheet, or leads' review line, and appear only inside a lead's working-with-me document and Session 1's instrument on the team home | Search every record on the team home and the OS surface for the four names; a hit outside a working-with-me document or the instrument fails the row | Brandon's seat |
| 121\. ## 19\. Instrument specifications

Specifications, never instruments. Nothing here is built, and no session builds any of it until the document methodology exists (`86ajgn2z5`). Each states what it is, whether Sŏn uses it, what it must contain, do, and refuse, where it lives and whether that is configuration, a build, or to confirm, who owns it and on what rhythm, and what it is gated on. Numbering is this page's own, I1 onward; earlier sessions' instruments are cited by session and number. The instruments her material proposes that Sŏn refuses come last, each with what does its work.

**I1. The brief's team slot list.** What it is: the fixed list of what the slot may carry (section 9.1), as an extension to Session 4's brief spine (S4 13.1) and Session 8's designation block (S8 `86akhcz4d`). Whether Sŏn uses it: yes; carryover `86akh67xe` asked for it. Must contain: the four items in priority with one sentence each on what the item is and who speaks it; the refused list; the ceiling as a reset parameter and the compressed-window rule; the record mark (which item ran, or dropped). Must do: sit after the readiness block and end at the scene trigger; survive a thirty-second brief by dropping whole; be the same list on the room designation's card; be spoken in the team's languages; feed row 119 and the slot count in section 15. Must refuse: an item about a person beyond a page fact; a script; a survey; an opener; a personal share; a lagging figure; an announced change; a build item; a fifth item. Where it lives: the brief's block on the OS surface and the room designation's card, a build. Who owns it: the owner of the room; every brief; the reviewing lead chooses the capture. Gated on: the document methodology; S4 I brief spine; `86akh3tg0` for the principle item; the chef ruling for the pass owner's line.

**I2. The whole-house gathering's team-making half.** What it is: the second half of Session 4's conditional gathering (S4 P38), specified in section 9.2. Whether Sŏn uses it: if the gathering is approved. Must contain: the five items in order (threads, what the house learned, the principles read back, coverage, one open question with its destination and window); the refused list; the schedule entry as a paid shift. Must do: follow Session 4's content on the house review's closed day; put the open question to the channel; feed row 126; carry nothing about a person beyond a page fact. Must refuse: an opener or closer, an icebreaker, the grid, a survey, a culture speech, an announced structure change, a lagging figure. Where it lives: the team home's gathering record, a build. Who owns it: the center; quarterly. Gated on: `86akh5uc7` and `86akh673u`; the document methodology; the closed day (`86akh6739`); principles version one for the read-back.

**I3. The destinations page.** What it is: one page on the team home stating where each speech act goes (section 6.4), delivered in the why block's sequence. Whether Sŏn uses it: yes; it is what makes "no topics are undiscussable" a rule a person can check. Must contain: a question (the mentor, the check-in, the channel); a friction (the check-in, the channel); a dissent (the hold's joint half-page; the upward question); a failure (the capture); a non-negotiable (both leads, that day); a concern about a lead (the holder ruled under `86akhb2jg`, and until then the entry reads "held"); the loop-closure windows; the rule that a topic with no destination is reported as one. Gated on: the document methodology; `86akhb2jg` for the lead's entry.

**I4. The designation's rotation floor.** What it is: the clause added to each designation's rule on the register (section 14.3), extending Session 8's designation entries (S8 18.9) and Session 9's recurrence rules (S9 I3). Must contain: the eligibility rule (readiness form, range card, no non-negotiable line); the floor in section 14.3's words; the stack's count per quarter as the read; the three branches at the reset (S9 P32); the refusals (no pay line, page mark, title, sheet field, reward, sanction).
