## 20\. Findings inside Sŏn's record

Twelve findings, each a conflict, a silence, or two accounts of the same thing, found by reading the white paper and both canon artifacts against each other with the environment, agency, safety, belonging for the team, meetings, and the playground as the question. The ledger's open questions and Sessions 2 to 9's findings (the six-tier difference and the Playground's tier at S2; the employee area's absence from canon's sequence at S7 19.11; the close window's length at S4; canon's judgment test against the documentation fix at S9 19.7; upward feedback's reader at S9 19.9) are not counted again; where one touches a finding it is named as adjacent. None is resolved here; where a section above supplied a working answer, the finding says which position holds it and marks it as the team's reading.

**20.1 Canon states the obligation for three parties and specifies it for one.** In one place: the Playground Philosophy is "for customers, founders, and employees" (Canon 1.0, section 01) and requires "Conditions for agency for customers, founders, and employees alike" (Deck 3.0, p.14). Elsewhere, on the same page: of Canon 1.0's six prohibitions and five requirements, nine are customer-facing, two touch the employee (training toward judgment; authority at the closest-to-customer position), and none touches a founder; the deck adds no list. Why it bears on the environment: the philosophy's employee half arrives with two mechanisms named and a claim about everything else, and its founder half with none, which is the honest starting point for Brandon's question. Who closes: canon's owner; section 2.3's ten conditions are the team's reading of what the employee half would specify. Silence, inside the narrow range.

**20.2 "Open enough to stay" is a condition in canon and retention is an output in the record.** In one place: a playground is "Clear enough to feel safe; open enough to stay" (Canon 1.0, section 01; Deck 3.0, p.14). Elsewhere: "Bandwidth, then joy, then retention, then results. This is the metabolic sequence" (WP p.12), retention third and produced by the two before it, and "the order is the decision" (Deck 3.0, p.4). Why it bears on the environment: if staying is a condition, the house builds for it directly and her belonging instruments have a place; if it is an output, the house builds bandwidth and joy and reads staying. Who closes: the founders, with `86akh3t00`; section 2.3 reads staying as the output and section 14 tests whether a direct mechanism is needed anyway, as the team's reading. Two accounts; canon against WP p.12.

**20.3 Culture is the elastic phase, and nothing in the record builds it.** In one place: "The elastic connective tissue is organizational culture: the connective flexibility that allows the structure to flex under stress without fracturing. Culture is not soft. It is the phase that keeps the strong phase from becoming brittle" (WP p.9). Elsewhere: every mechanism Part II names is an anchor point (domain ownership, the seat, the range, the path) or the nervous system (the stack, the indicators, the channel); the record names no mechanism whose output is the elastic phase, and its one sentence on the phase's production is that culture "takes time and organizational development a competitor cannot shortcut" (WP p.23). Why it bears on the environment: the record's own material science says the anchors alone "shatter under stress" (WP p.9), and the environment is where the other phase would be built. Who closes: the record's author; sections 3 and 14 read the elastic phase as the outcome of the ten conditions and the mentor as its one placed carrier, as the team's reading. Silence; needs p.9 against Part II.

**20.4 Belonging is built in full for the customer and as a break space for the team.** In one place: Part III builds belonging from the first visit to the fifth, "being known by someone, not just recognized by a system," "People return to places where they feel safe, known, and respected" (WP pp. 25 to 26). Elsewhere: the team's version is "A real employee area with secure lockers and a comfortable break space is not a perk. It is basic dignity" (WP p.20), and the labor-as-asset section imports "retention systems" from other sectors (WP p.16) without naming what the team belongs to. Why it bears on the environment: the condition the record says makes a customer stay is written for the customer and not for the person serving them. Who closes: the record's author, with the founders on whether a team-side belonging mechanism exists at all (P22, P12); section 3.6's "partial, thin among peers" is the team's reading. Two accounts; needs Part III against Part II.

**20.5 Blame absorption runs one way, and the one failure the record treats as a person's has no path.** In one place: "Management absorbs blame from staff" (WP p.17) and, for the customer, "the customer should never feel at fault, even when they are" (WP p.26). Elsewhere: "No Toxicity Ever" (Canon 1.0, section 01) is the one act the record and canon treat as a person's, and nothing in the record says where it goes, who reads it, or what the process's share of it is. Why it bears on safety: the environment's safety half rests on the failure being the process's, and the record never says where that stops. Who closes: the founders with Sessions 12, 14, and 15; section 6.2's rule that the flag goes to both leads that day and is said in no room is the team's reading of the environment's part only. Silence; needs p.17 against p.26 and canon.

**20.6 The record's measure of psychological safety is a survey, and the program refused surveys.** In one place: "engagement results across psychological safety and values alignment" (WP p.23). Elsewhere: the leading indicators are "tracked regularly rather than annually" (WP p.22) and Session 9 refused the survey as a form (S9 P5, I10). Why it bears on the environment: the record's stated read of safety has no instrument the program accepts, and the substitute (the capture rate, the error-reporting rate, the pulse) has no baseline. Who closes: the founders, with `86akh5u9x`; section 6.3 is the team's reading. Two accounts; inside the narrow range.

**20.7 A private post-mortem and a gathered story of daily problem-solving are the same event under two rules.** In one place: "Post-mortems are private and process-focused" (WP p.17). Elsewhere: cultural measurement gathers "Stories of how the culture shows up in daily problem-solving" (WP p.23). Why it bears on the environment: the brief's slot carries "what the system learned" as process (section 9.1), and the record has one rule that keeps the event private and another that tells it; the slot's item is written to the first rule and the gathering's second item to the second. Who closes: the record's author; the team's reading is that the process is told and the incident is not. Two accounts; inside the narrow range.

**20.8 The pre-service window has a length in canon and none in the record.** In one place: canon's pre-service scene is "30 to 45 minute programmatic scene before first seating. Person-triggered" (Canon 1.0, section 06). Elsewhere: the record's window is "Beginning of shift, prepare for the customer" (WP p.26) and "the pre-shift briefing" as equal in importance to the signature dish (WP p.20), with no length; the check-in is placed in it (S4 P15), the brief's slot ends at the scene trigger (section 9.1), and a meal would sit in it (P12). Why it bears on the environment: three of the ten conditions spend the window's minutes and the record never says how many there are. Who closes: the founders with the Realist's read at the first reset; adjacent to S4's close-window finding. Two accounts; canon against WP p.26.

**20.9 The staff meal is absent from the record and both canon artifacts.** In one place: nowhere. Elsewhere: her Table 8 names a meal as the plainest team-focused activity (Book p.308), and the industry runs one before every service. Why it bears on the environment: it is the one team mechanism on her list that passes the entry test on its face and the record is silent. Who closes: the founders with the chef (P12, P13). Silence; needs the whole record.

**20.10 Canon's lexicon applies in all contexts, and peer recognition is written by the team in the moment.** In one place: the forbidden lexicon is "Forbidden in all contexts, no exceptions" (Canon 1.0, section 09), the language constant applies to "any internal communication" (Canon 1.0, section 01; Deck 3.0, p.5), and no exclamation points appear "in any written brand voice context" (Canon 1.0, section 09). Elsewhere: "Peer recognition runs through a platform that lets colleagues acknowledge excellence in the moment" (WP p.19), read aloud at the brief "not editorialized" (S4 P10). Why it bears on the environment: whether a server's own words on the platform are a brand surface is unstated, and if they are, the one mechanism that carries a peer's voice is governed by rules written for copy. Who closes: canon's owner with Session 11; the team's reading is that the language constant applies and the lexicon does not, and it is marked as held. Two accounts; canon against WP p.19.

**20.11 The Maitre d owns "the emotional standard of the room," and no versioned document holds it.** In one place: the Maitre d owns "Service culture and the emotional standard of the room" (WP p.10). Elsewhere: canon's service model holds the step-back architecture, the floor authority, and the register (Canon 1.0, section 08), a living document changes "by versioned decision, never by drift" (Deck 3.0, p.94), and canon's owner is held (`86akh3t3y`). Why it bears on the tight edge: a standard a seat owns and no document holds is the standard most likely to become a lead's personal rule (section 4.1). Who closes: the founders with canon's owner; section 4.1's guard, that a rule with no version is not a rule, is the team's reading. Silence; needs p.10 against canon and the versioning rule.

**20.12 "Employees are the users," and every user-facing mechanism was written before a user existed.** In one place: "Restaurant founders build systems for themselves without realizing it, then blame employees when those systems do not work for anyone else. Sŏn has done it too, which is how the team knows the trap... Employees are the users" (WP p.17). Elsewhere, on the same page: every mechanism on this page and Sessions 3 to 9's was designed by the founders and this program before any employee read one, and the loop that corrects it, "continuous feedback loops so the tools evolve based on real usage," starts on the first shift. Why it bears on the environment: the environment is, until the first reset, exactly the founder-built system the record warns against, and the only read of that is the first run's cannot-read list (S9 P22) and the first reset. Who closes: the first reset, on the first quarter's channel and check-in lines; the team's reading is that the freeze protects the loop from the founders and the reset is where the users' read lands. Two accounts of the same page; inside the narrow range.

Twelve findings: five silences, six two-account conflicts, and one two-account conflict inside one page. Four of the twelve (20.1, 20.6, 20.7, 20.12) sit inside canon's Playground page or the white paper's people sections (WP pp. 16 to 23) and would surface from a narrow read. The other eight would not: 20.2 needs canon against WP p.12; 20.3 needs p.9 against Part II; 20.4 needs Part III against Part II; 20.5 needs p.17 against p.26 and canon; 20.8 needs canon's spatial section against p.26; 20.9 needs the whole record to know a thing is absent; 20.10 needs canon's verbal identity against p.19; 20.11 needs p.10 against canon's service model and the deck's versioning rule. A session that read the Playground page and the people sections and stopped would have found that canon specifies the employee half twice and the founder half never, and missed that canon and the record disagree about whether staying is a condition or an output, that the record's culture is a phase nothing builds, that belonging is written for the customer, that the room's emotional standard has no document, and that the one team mechanism the industry runs daily is absent from every page.

**P44 (Recommended).** The twelve findings are filed as stated, each routed to who closes it. None is resolved here; where a section above supplied a working answer it is the team's reading and marked as such. 20.3, 20.4, and 20.7 are routed to the record's author; 20.2, 20.5, 20.6, 20.8, 20.9, and 20.12 to the founders with the open items they extend; 20.1, 20.10, and 20.11 to canon's owner and the versioning authority, 20.10 with Session 11.

## 21\. The verdict

Brandon's question was whether the Playground Philosophy, on the employee side, is mechanisms or a slogan. The answer is neither whole, and the page says which parts are which.

**Built, as mechanisms.** Legible rules (the sheet, the range card, the why block, the team home, the change line). A stated range (the register and the floor's authority, with its money values open). Safety to err (blame the process, the capture, no verdict anywhere). A path (the invisible advocate, the tracks, the three seats). These four are the record's own machinery, and every one of them refuses the manager her chapter assumes. Two are gated on things not yet built (the charter's why block; the learning platform) and one on values not yet set; none is gated on an idea.

**Partial.** Judgment beyond procedure: the architecture reaches it and reads it once, and nothing reads it after except range use. Safety to speak: three of four speech acts have destinations, and a concern about a lead has none the lead does not hold until `86akhb2jg` closes. Being known: whole by the house through the lead, thin among the team. Time not taken: designed in and priced, and unreadable at the close and in the labor model until the window's length, the cultural labor score, and slack are stated. A say in the rules: whole on the process, indirect on the rules until the floor is asked in the one room it is in.

**Slogan today.** A place of their own: promised as "a precondition for presence" and placed on no drawing.
